  days_from_planned varchar [note: 'Signed integer representing the deviation in days between the actual visit date and the planned visit date (actual minus planned). Negative values indicate early visits; positive values indicate late visits. Zero indicates on-schedule.']
  duration_minutes varchar [note: 'Total duration of the visit in minutes from check-in to check-out as recorded in the CTMS or EDC. Used for site capacity planning, resource utilization analysis, and subject burden assessment.']
  early_termination_reason varchar [note: 'Reason for early termination of the visit or the subject\'s participation, applicable when visit_type is \'early_termination\'. Captures clinical, safety, or administrative reasons per protocol requirements.']
  informed_consent_verified boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a valid, signed Informed Consent Form (ICF) was confirmed on file prior to this visit (True) or not (False). Critical GCP compliance requirement; absence may constitute a major protocol deviation.']
  is_scheduled boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this visit was a protocol-scheduled visit (True) or an unscheduled/ad-hoc visit not defined in the protocol schedule of assessments (False). Unscheduled visits may indicate safety events or protocol deviations.']
  is_unblinded boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the treatment assignment was unblinded at or prior to this visit (True) or the subject remained blinded (False). Relevant for double-blind studies and impacts data integrity assessments.']
  missed_reason varchar [note: 'Free-text or coded reason explaining why a scheduled visit was missed by the subject (e.g., subject unavailable, adverse event, travel, withdrew consent, site closure). Populated only when visit_status is \'missed\'.']
  missed_reason_code varchar [note: 'Standardized coded value for the reason a scheduled visit was missed, aligned with sponsor or protocol-defined coding scheme. Complements missed_reason free text for structured analytics and regulatory submissions.']
  notes varchar [note: 'Free-text clinical or operational notes recorded by the site staff or CRA regarding this visit, including observations about subject condition, procedural issues, or site-specific circumstances. Sourced from the source system or Medidata Rave.']
  planned_visit_date date [note: 'The target date on which the visit was scheduled to occur per the protocol-defined visit schedule, calculated from the subject\'s reference date (e.g., randomization date or first dose date). Used to compute visit window compliance.']
  protocol_deviation_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this visit resulted in a protocol deviation (True), such as a visit outside the allowed window, missed required assessments, or procedural non-compliance. Triggers downstream protocol deviation record creation in the compliance domain.']
  query_count varchar [note: 'Number of open data discrepancy queries (DCFs) associated with this visit\'s eCRF data in the EDC system. Used for data quality monitoring and site performance tracking. Non-zero values may block database lock.']
  source_system_visit_key varchar [note: 'The native primary key or unique identifier for this visit record in the originating source system (e.g., Medidata Rave visit OID, Siebel CTMS visit row ID).']
  study_day varchar [note: 'The relative study day on which the visit occurred, calculated from the subject\'s reference start date per CDISC convention (Day 1 = reference date; Day -1 = day before; no Day 0). Maps to SVSTDY in CDISC SDTM SV domain.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent modification to this subject visit record in the source system or Silver layer. Required for change tracking, audit trail compliance, and incremental data pipeline processing.']
  visit_code varchar [note: 'Protocol-defined alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the visit within the study schedule (e.g., SCR, BL, V01, V02, ET, EOS). Maps to VISITNUM/VISIT in CDISC SDTM SV domain. Used as the externally-known business identifier for the visit.']
  visit_number varchar [note: 'Sequential numeric identifier for the visit as defined in the study protocol schedule of assessments. Maps directly to VISITNUM in CDISC SDTM SV domain. Used for ordering visits chronologically within a subject\'s participation.']
  visit_status varchar [note: 'Current completion status of the visit indicating whether the subject attended and completed all required assessments, missed the visit entirely, partially completed assessments, had the visit rescheduled, or the visit was cancelled.']
  visit_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the visit by its role in the study protocol lifecycle. Drives SDTM SV domain population and visit compliance analytics. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: screening|baseline|treatment|follow_up|unscheduled|early_termination|end_of_study — promote to']
  week varchar [note: 'The nominal study week associated with this visit as defined in the protocol schedule of assessments (e.g., Week 1, Week 4, Week 12). Used for time-point labeling in biostatistical analyses and ADaM dataset derivations.']
  window_close_date date [note: 'The latest acceptable date for the visit to occur per the protocol-defined visit window (planned date plus the allowed late deviation in days). Used to determine visit window compliance status.']
  window_compliance_status varchar [note: 'Indicates whether the actual visit date fell within the protocol-defined visit window, occurred early (before window open), occurred late (after window close), was missed entirely, or is not applicable (e.g., unscheduled visits).']
  window_open_date date [note: 'The earliest acceptable date for the visit to occur per the protocol-defined visit window (planned date minus the allowed early deviation in days). Used to determine visit window compliance status.']

  Note: 'Single owner of a subject\'s protocol-scheduled study visit (clinical visit).'
}

Table subject.deviation {
  deviation_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique surrogate identifier for each protocol deviation record associated with a trial subject. Primary key for the subject_deviation data product in the Silver Layer lakehouse.']
  capa_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the formal Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) record in MasterControl that was initiated as a result of this deviation. Enables traceability between deviations and the quality management system.']
  dispensing_record_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to supply.dispensing_record. Business justification: Protocol deviations frequently originate from incorrect dispensing events (wrong kit, wrong dose, wrong visit window).']
  document_sop_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to document.document_sop. Business justification: Protocol deviations are assessed against the specific SOP that was violated or not followed.']
  eligibility_criterion_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to study.eligibility_criterion. Business justification: Eligibility violations are a distinct deviation category requiring direct linkage to the specific criterion violated.']
  enrollment_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to subject.enrollment. Business justification: Protocol deviations are enrollment-specific events — they occur within the context of a subject\'s participation in a specific study enrollment.']
  epoch_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to study.epoch. Business justification: DSMB safety reports and deviation trend analyses require epoch-level stratification of protocol deviations.']
  ethics_submission_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to compliance.ethics_submission. Business justification: Subject deviations with irb_iec_reportable_flag=true must be reported to the IRB/IEC via a formal ethics submission.']
  investigational_site_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the investigational site where the deviation occurred. Used for site-level deviation trending, monitoring, and risk assessment.']
  irb_iec_approval_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to site.irb_iec_approval. Business justification: When subject_deviation.irb_iec_reportable_flag=true, the specific IRB/IEC approval record to which the deviation must be reported must be directly identified.']
  irt_transaction_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to randomization.irt_transaction. Business justification: Protocol deviations are frequently caused by IRT/RTSM errors (wrong randomization number issued, incorrect kit dispensed).']
  kit_assignment_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to randomization.kit_assignment. Business justification: Kit assignment errors (expired kit dispensed, wrong kit number, temperature excursion) are a primary source of protocol deviations.']
  kit_inventory_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to supply.kit_inventory. Business justification: Deviations involving wrong kit dispensing (incorrect randomization number, wrong treatment arm) must reference the specific kit_inventory record for IMP accountability investigations and']
  lab_result_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to laboratory.lab_result. Business justification: Protocol deviations are frequently identified through abnormal lab results (e.g., subject continued dosing despite creatinine exceeding stopping rule).']
  regulatory_protocol_amendment_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to regulatory.protocol_amendment. Business justification: A subject deviation is assessed against the protocol version in effect at the time of occurrence.']
  serious_adverse_event_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to safety.serious_adverse_event. Business justification: Protocol deviations often trigger or result from SAEs; investigators must cross-reference deviations with SAE reports for causality assessment and regulatory reporting per 21 CFR']
  specimen_collection_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to laboratory.specimen_collection. Business justification: Protocol deviation root-cause analysis requires tracing which specific specimen collection event (wrong tube, missed timepoint, incorrect volume) triggered the deviation.']
  study_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the clinical study (protocol) under which this deviation was identified. Links the deviation to the governing protocol and sponsor.']
  study_site_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to site.study_site. Business justification: Deviation reports and supporting documentation must be filed in the Investigator Site File as GCP-required essential documents.']
  submission_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to regulatory.submission. Business justification: Regulatory-reportable deviations (regulatory_reportable_flag=true) must be traceable to the specific regulatory submission in which they were reported to the health authority.']
  susar_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to safety.susar. Business justification: SUSARs require immediate protocol deviation assessment for expedited regulatory reporting (EU CT Regulation 536/2014, FDA IND Safety Reporting).']
  tmf_document_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to document.tmf_document. Business justification: Regulatory traceability requires mapping subject deviations to the protocol amendment version in effect at occurrence.']
  trial_subject_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the trial subject (patient) for whom this protocol deviation was recorded. Core party reference linking the deviation to the enrolled participant.']
  visit_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to subject.subject_visit. Business justification: Protocol deviations are frequently identified at or associated with a specific study visit.']
  workflow_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to document.workflow. Business justification: Protocol deviations trigger CAPA document workflows requiring sponsor review, PI acknowledgment, and IRB/IEC notification documents.']
  closed_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The precise date and time when the deviation record was formally closed in the quality management system. Provides higher precision than resolution_date for audit and compliance reporting.']
  comments varchar [note: 'Free-text field for additional comments, clarifications, or contextual notes related to the deviation that do not fit into structured fields. May include reviewer notes, sponsor feedback, or monitoring observations.']
  corrective_action_description varchar [note: 'Narrative description of the immediate corrective action taken to address the deviation and prevent recurrence at the subject or site level. Distinct from the formal CAPA process which is tracked separately in MasterControl.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this deviation record was first created in the source system. Supports ALCOA+ audit trail requirements and data lineage tracking per 21 CFR Part 11 and ICH E6(R2).']
  data_integrity_impact varchar [note: 'Assessment of whether the deviation compromised the integrity of study data collected from the subject. Informs decisions on data exclusion, sensitivity analyses, and per-protocol (PP) population definitions.']
  deviation_category varchar [note: 'Classification of the deviation by severity and impact. \'Major\' deviations significantly affect subject safety or data integrity; \'important\' deviations may affect subject rights or study data; \'minor\' deviations have minimal impact.']
  deviation_description varchar [note: 'Detailed narrative description of the specific deviation that occurred, including what protocol requirement was not met, the circumstances, and any relevant context.']
  deviation_number varchar [note: 'Externally-known, human-readable unique identifier for the deviation record as assigned by the Clinical Trial Management System (CTMS) or MasterControl. Used for cross-system referencing, regulatory submissions, and audit trail purposes.']
  deviation_status varchar [note: 'Current workflow lifecycle state of the deviation record. Tracks progression from initial identification through review, resolution, and closure. Drives operational dashboards and compliance monitoring in the source system and MasterControl.']
  identified_date date [note: 'The calendar date on which the deviation was first identified or discovered, which may differ from the occurrence date. Used to calculate detection lag and assess monitoring effectiveness.']
  irb_iec_reportable_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this deviation must be reported to the Institutional Review Board (IRB) or Independent Ethics Committee (IEC) overseeing the study. Separate from regulatory authority reportability. True = must report to IRB/IEC.']
  occurrence_date date [note: 'The calendar date on which the protocol deviation actually occurred. This is the principal real-world event date, distinct from the date the deviation was identified or reported. Critical for ALCOA+ compliance and regulatory timelines.']
  pi_aware_date date [note: 'The date on which the Principal Investigator (PI) was informed of the deviation. Used to track compliance with site notification requirements.']
  pi_aware_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the Principal Investigator (PI) at the site has been made aware of this deviation. True = PI has been informed. Required for GCP compliance as the PI bears ultimate responsibility for conduct of the trial at the site.']
  protocol_section_reference varchar [note: 'Reference to the specific section, clause, or requirement number within the approved study protocol that was deviated from (e.g., \'Section 6.3.2 - Inclusion Criteria\'). Enables precise traceability to the protocol document.']
  regulatory_reportable_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this deviation must be reported to a regulatory authority (FDA, EMA, PMDA, etc.), IRB/IEC, or sponsor per applicable regulations and the study protocol. True = reportable; False = not reportable. Drives regulatory submission workflows.']
  reported_date date [note: 'The date on which the deviation was formally reported to the sponsor, IRB/IEC, or regulatory authority as applicable. Used to track compliance with reporting timelines mandated by GCP and applicable regulations.']
  resolution_date date [note: 'The date on which the deviation was formally resolved and closed in the quality management system. Used to calculate time-to-resolution metrics and assess site responsiveness.']
  root_cause varchar [note: 'Narrative description of the underlying root cause of the deviation as determined through investigation. Used to inform corrective and preventive actions (CAPA) and systemic quality improvement. Captured in MasterControl.']
  root_cause_category varchar [note: 'Categorical classification of the root cause to enable trending and systemic analysis across deviations. Categories align with standard quality management frameworks used in MasterControl.']
  sdtm_domain varchar [note: 'The CDISC SDTM domain to which this deviation maps for regulatory submission. Protocol deviations are mapped to the DV (Protocol Deviations) domain per CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide.']
  source_system_record_reference varchar [note: 'The native record identifier from the originating source system (the source system or MasterControl). Enables bidirectional traceability between the lakehouse Silver Layer and the operational system of record.']
  sponsor_notified_date date [note: 'The date on which the sponsor was formally notified of the deviation. Used to verify compliance with contractual and regulatory notification timelines.']
  sponsor_notified_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the study sponsor has been formally notified of this deviation. True = sponsor has been notified. Required per GCP obligations for sponsor oversight of investigational sites.']
  subject_continuation_decision varchar [note: 'Decision regarding the subject\'s continued participation in the study following the deviation. Informs subject disposition tracking and intent-to-treat (ITT) and per-protocol (PP) population assignments.']
  subject_rights_impact varchar [note: 'Assessment of whether the deviation affected the rights or well-being of the trial subject, including informed consent procedures, privacy protections, or voluntary participation rights.']
  subject_safety_impact varchar [note: 'Assessment of whether the deviation had an impact on subject safety. \'None\' indicates no safety impact; \'potential\' indicates possible but unconfirmed impact; \'confirmed\' indicates a verified safety impact.']
  type_code varchar [note: 'Standardized code identifying the specific type of protocol deviation (e.g., eligibility criteria violation, missed visit, incorrect dosing, prohibited medication use, consent procedure deviation).']
  type_description varchar [note: 'Human-readable label corresponding to the deviation_type_code, providing a plain-language description of the deviation type for reporting and review purposes.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this deviation record was most recently modified. Supports change tracking, audit trail compliance, and incremental data loading in the Databricks Silver Layer.']

  Note: 'Transactional record of a protocol deviation identified for a subject, capturing deviation category (major, minor, important), deviation type code, description, date of occurrence, date identified, root cause, impact on subject safety and data integrity'
}

  study_completion_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the subject completed the study per protocol (True) or did not complete (False). Drives CONSORT flow diagram completion counts and CSR disposition summary tables.']
  subject_number varchar [note: 'Externally-known alphanumeric identifier assigned to the subject at the site (e.g., 001-001). Corresponds to SDTM USUBJID or site-assigned subject number. BUSINESS_IDENTIFIER for this transaction. Sourced from Medidata Rave EDC.']
  term varchar [note: 'Standardized disposition term describing the subject\'s formal study milestone (e.g., COMPLETED, SCREEN FAILURE, DISCONTINUED, WITHDRAWN BY SUBJECT, LOST TO FOLLOW-UP, DEATH). Corresponds to SDTM DSTERM.']
  timestamp timestamp [note: 'Full ISO 8601 timestamp of the disposition event when time-of-day precision is available. Supplements disposition_date for events requiring precise timing (e.g., time of death, time of last dose). Corresponds to SDTM DSSTDTC full datetime.']

  Note: 'Transactional record capturing each formal disposition milestone of a subject through the study lifecycle (screened, enrolled, randomized, completed, discontinued, withdrawn, lost to follow-up, death).'

  assessment_number varchar [note: 'Externally-known business identifier for this eligibility assessment, typically generated by the EDC system (Medidata Rave or the source system Used for cross-system traceability and audit trail references.']
  assessment_result varchar [note: 'Outcome of the eligibility criterion assessment for this subject. MET indicates the criterion was satisfied; NOT MET indicates failure; NOT ASSESSED indicates the criterion was not evaluated. Maps to CDISC SDTM IE.IEORRES.']
  assessment_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Precise date and time at which the eligibility criterion assessment was recorded in the EDC system. Supports ALCOA+ contemporaneous documentation requirements and 21 CFR Part 11 audit trail.']
  assessor_role varchar [note: 'Role of the site staff member who performed the eligibility assessment (e.g., Principal Investigator, Sub-Investigator, Clinical Research Coordinator). Required for GCP delegation log compliance.']
  comments varchar [note: 'Free-text comments or clinical notes entered by the assessor regarding this eligibility criterion assessment. May include clarifications, borderline findings, or contextual information relevant to the eligibility decision.']
  data_entry_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when this eligibility assessment record was first entered into the EDC system. Distinct from assessment_timestamp (when assessment occurred). Supports ALCOA+ contemporaneous data entry monitoring.']
  data_source_system varchar [note: 'Identifies the operational system of record from which this eligibility assessment record was sourced (Medidata Rave EDC or the source system Supports data lineage and reconciliation in the Silver layer.']
  edc_record_reference varchar [note: 'Source system record identifier from the EDC platform (Medidata Rave or the source system for this eligibility assessment entry. Enables traceability back to the source system for SDV and audit.']
  irb_iec_approval_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether IRB/IEC approval is required for the waiver or exception associated with this eligibility criterion assessment. Drives regulatory workflow routing.']
  last_modified_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when this eligibility assessment record was last updated in the source EDC system. Required for 21 CFR Part 11 audit trail and ALCOA+ data integrity compliance.']
  lock_status varchar [note: 'Data lock status of this eligibility assessment record in the EDC system. LOCKED records cannot be modified without an audit-trailed unlock. Supports Database Lock (DBL) readiness and 21 CFR Part 11 compliance.']
  not_met_reason varchar [note: 'Free-text or coded reason explaining why the subject did not meet this eligibility criterion. Populated when assessment_result is NOT MET. Supports clinical review and protocol deviation analysis.']
  overall_eligibility_status varchar [note: 'Overall eligibility determination for the subject based on the complete set of inclusion/exclusion criteria assessments. Drives subject enrollment decision. Lifecycle status for this assessment record.']

  query_open_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether an open data discrepancy query exists against this eligibility assessment record in the EDC system. Supports data cleaning status monitoring and DBL readiness tracking.']
  re_screening_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this eligibility assessment is part of a re-screening attempt following an initial screen failure. Supports enrollment funnel analytics and re-screening rate KPI reporting.']
  screen_failure_reason varchar [note: 'Coded or free-text reason for screen failure when the overall eligibility determination is INELIGIBLE. Used for enrollment analytics, site performance reporting, and protocol feasibility review.']
  sdtm_domain varchar [note: 'CDISC SDTM domain code for this eligibility assessment record. Always \'IE\' (Inclusion/Exclusion Criteria Not Met) for regulatory submission datasets. Supports SDTM mapping and NDA/BLA/MAA submission.']
  sdtm_sequence_number varchar [note: 'CDISC SDTM sequence number (IESEQ) uniquely identifying this record within the IE domain for a given subject. Required for regulatory submission dataset construction.']
  sdv_date date [note: 'Date on which Source Data Verification (SDV) was completed for this eligibility assessment record by the CRA. Null when SDV has not yet been performed.']
  sdv_status varchar [note: 'Status of Source Data Verification (SDV) performed by the Clinical Research Associate (CRA) for this eligibility assessment record. Tracks monitoring compliance per the monitoring plan.']
  source_data_reference varchar [note: 'Reference to the source document or data entry (e.g., medical record number, lab report ID, physical examination note) that supports the eligibility criterion assessment. Required for Source Data Verification (SDV) by CRA.']
  waiver_approval_date date [note: 'Date on which the sponsor or IRB/IEC approved the protocol exception or waiver for this eligibility criterion. Null when no waiver was requested or waiver was denied.']
  waiver_justification varchar [note: 'Free-text clinical or scientific justification provided by the investigator for requesting a protocol exception or waiver for this eligibility criterion. Required for regulatory audit trail.']
  waiver_requested boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a protocol deviation waiver or exception was requested for this criterion when the subject did not meet it. True when a waiver request has been submitted to the sponsor or IRB/IEC.']
  waiver_status varchar [note: 'Current status of the protocol-specified exception or waiver request for this eligibility criterion. Applicable only when waiver_requested is True. Tracks sponsor or IRB/IEC decision.']

  Note: 'Transactional record of the inclusion/exclusion criteria assessment performed for a subject during screening. Captures each criterion code, criterion text, assessment result (met/not met/not assessed), assessment date, assessor identity, and overall'
}

Table subject.status_history {
  status_history_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique surrogate identifier for each subject status transition record in the lifecycle history table. Primary key for the subject_status_history data product.']
  consent_subject_consent_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to consent.subject_consent. Business justification: Status transitions (screening→enrolled, enrolled→withdrawn) are driven by consent events.']
  disposition_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to subject.disposition. Business justification: A subject status transition is often triggered by a formal disposition milestone (e.g., the \'completed\' status transition corresponds to a disposition record with']
  eligibility_assessment_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to subject.eligibility_assessment. Business justification: Status transitions to \'eligible\', \'screen failed\', or \'ineligible\' are directly triggered by the outcome of an eligibility assessment.']
  enrollment_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to subject.enrollment. Business justification: Subject status transitions (screening, enrolled, randomized, completed, withdrawn) are enrollment-specific lifecycle events.']
  epoch_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to study.study_epoch. Business justification: Subject status transitions (screening, randomization, treatment, follow-up, completion) occur within defined study epochs.']
  investigational_site_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the investigational site at which the subject status transition was recorded. Supports site-level enrollment flow analysis and monitoring.']
  protocol_deviation_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the specific protocol deviation record associated with this status transition, when protocol_deviation_flag is True. Links to the compliance.protocol_deviation product for full deviation details.']
  randomization_assignment_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to subject.randomization_assignment. Business justification: When a subject transitions to \'randomized\' status, the specific randomization_assignment that triggered the transition should be traceable from the status history record.']
  regulatory_protocol_amendment_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to regulatory.protocol_amendment. Business justification: Status transitions triggered by protocol amendments (reconsent required, arm reassignment, eligibility re-evaluation) must reference the causative amendment for regulatory audit']
  serious_adverse_event_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to safety.serious_adverse_event. Business justification: Subject status transitions are often triggered by SAEs. Audit trail requirements per 21 CFR Part 11 and GCP mandate linking status changes to causative SAE events for regulatory']
  study_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the clinical study (protocol) under which this subject status transition occurred. Links the history record to the governing study protocol.']
  subject_randomization_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to randomization.subject_randomization. Business justification: ICH E6 R2 audit trail requires status transitions (Randomized, Re-randomized, Unblinded) to be traceable to the specific IRT event that triggered them.']
  susar_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to safety.susar. Business justification: SUSAR events mandate immediate status transitions and blinding decisions. Regulatory timelines (7-day fatal/life-threatening, 15-day other) require traceable status history linked to specific']
  tmf_document_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to document.tmf_document. Business justification: Terminal status transitions (withdrawal, death, completion) generate TMF essential documents.']
  treatment_arm_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to randomization.treatment_arm. Business justification: Subject status transitions (randomized, on-treatment, completed, withdrawn) are arm-specific.']
  trial_subject_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the trial subject (participant) whose enrollment lifecycle status changed. Core party reference for this event log record.']
  unblinding_request_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to randomization.unblinding_request. Business justification: Emergency unblinding events directly trigger subject status transitions (e.g., from on-treatment to withdrawn or unblinded).']
  visit_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to subject.subject_visit. Business justification: A subject status transition (e.g., \'completed\', \'withdrawn\', \'screen failed\') is typically triggered at or recorded during a specific protocol visit.']
  approval_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time at which the status transition was formally approved or electronically signed by the authorized user. Distinct from transition_timestamp (when the event occurred) and created_timestamp (when the record was created).']
  comments varchar [note: 'Free-text field for additional clinical or administrative comments related to this status transition, entered by the site staff or sponsor. Supports contextual documentation for audit trail completeness per ALCOA+ standards.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time at which this status history record was first created in the data lakehouse Silver layer. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and ALCOA+ contemporaneous documentation requirements.']
  disposition_category varchar [note: 'High-level classification of the disposition event type associated with this status transition. Used for regulatory reporting in the CDISC SDTM DS domain and for subject flow summaries in Clinical Study Reports (CSRs).']
  irb_iec_approval_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this status transition required prior approval from the Institutional Review Board (IRB) or Independent Ethics Committee (IEC) (e.g., re-consent due to protocol amendment). True = IRB/IEC approval was required.']
  is_blinded boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the subject\'s treatment assignment was blinded at the time of this status transition. True = blinded (treatment identity concealed); False = unblinded (treatment identity known).']
  is_terminal_status boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the new_status represents a terminal (end-state) disposition for the subject in this study. True = the subject has reached a final state (completed, withdrawn, screen-failed, lost-to-follow-up) with no further expected transitions.']
  itt_population_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the subject was included in the Intent-to-Treat (ITT) analysis population at the time of this status transition. Supports biostatistical analysis population tracking per the Statistical Analysis Plan (the source system).']
  new_status varchar [note: 'The subject\'s enrollment lifecycle status after this transition event. Represents the current state the subject entered as a result of this change. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE']
  pp_population_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the subject was included in the Per Protocol (PP) analysis population at the time of this status transition. Supports biostatistical analysis population tracking per the Statistical Analysis Plan (the source system).']
  prior_status varchar [note: 'The subject\'s enrollment lifecycle status immediately before this transition event. Together with new_status, defines the state transition vector for longitudinal subject flow analysis.']
  protocol_deviation_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a protocol deviation (PD) was associated with or triggered this status transition. True = a protocol deviation is linked to this transition event. Supports GCP compliance monitoring and regulatory inspection readiness.']
  safety_population_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the subject was included in the safety analysis population at the time of this status transition (i.e., received at least one dose of investigational product). Supports safety reporting and TEAE analysis.']
  screen_failure_reason varchar [note: 'Specific reason why the subject failed screening and did not proceed to enrollment. Populated only when new_status = \'screen-failed\'. Used for site feasibility analysis, protocol amendment decisions, and enrollment optimization.']
  source_system_record_key varchar [note: 'The native primary key or unique identifier of this status transition record in the originating source system (the source system or Medidata Rave). Enables traceability back to the system of record for reconciliation and audit purposes.']
  study_day varchar [note: 'The relative study day on which the status transition occurred, calculated from the subject\'s reference start date (typically first dose date). Negative values indicate pre-treatment days. Aligns with CDISC SDTM timing variable conventions.']
  subject_number varchar [note: 'The externally-known alphanumeric subject identifier assigned at enrollment (e.g., site-sequential number such as \'001-001\'). Used in regulatory submissions, eCRFs, and audit trails to identify the participant without revealing personal identity.']
  transition_date date [note: 'The calendar date on which the subject\'s status transition occurred in the real-world clinical context. This is the principal business event date used for enrollment timelines, regulatory reporting, and subject flow analysis.']
  transition_reason varchar [note: 'Free-text narrative describing the clinical or administrative reason for the subject status change (e.g., \'Subject met all inclusion/exclusion criteria\', \'Subject withdrew consent\', \'Adverse event led to discontinuation\').']
  transition_reason_code varchar [note: 'Standardized coded value for the transition reason, aligned with CDISC SDTM DS domain disposition event codes (e.g., \'COMPLETED\', \'WITHDRAWAL BY SUBJECT\', \'ADVERSE EVENT\', \'SCREEN FAILURE\'). Enables structured analysis and regulatory submission mapping.']
  transition_sequence varchar [note: 'Sequential ordinal number of this status transition within the subject\'s complete enrollment lifecycle history. Enables chronological ordering of all transitions for a given subject within a study. Starts at 1 for the first recorded transition.']
  transition_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The precise date and time (with timezone) at which the subject status transition was recorded in the source system (the source system or Medidata Rave). Supports 21 CFR Part 11 audit trail requirements and ALCOA+ contemporaneous documentation standards.']
  triggered_by_system varchar [note: 'Identifies whether the status transition was triggered by a human user or an automated system process, and which source system initiated it (the source system Medidata Rave, IRT/RTSM). Supports data lineage and audit trail requirements.']
  triggered_by_user_role varchar [note: 'The clinical role of the user who triggered this status transition (e.g., CRC - Clinical Research Coordinator, CRA - Clinical Research Associate, PI - Principal Investigator). Supports audit trail completeness and role-based accountability per GCP.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time at which this status history record was last modified in the data lakehouse Silver layer. Supports change tracking, audit trail completeness, and data quality monitoring per 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ standards.']
  withdrawal_reason varchar [note: 'Specific reason for subject withdrawal or discontinuation from the study. Populated when new_status is \'withdrawn\' or \'discontinued\'. Categorized per CDISC SDTM DS domain controlled terminology (e.g., \'ADVERSE EVENT\', \'WITHDRAWAL BY SUBJECT\', \'LOST TO']

  Note: 'Lifecycle history table tracking every status transition of a trial subject across the enrollment lifecycle (e.g., pre-screened → screened → screen-failed → enrolled → randomized → on-treatment → completed → withdrawn).'
}

Table subject.demographic {
  demographic_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique surrogate identifier for each subject demographic record in the silver layer lakehouse. Primary key for the demographic data product.']
  age_unit_codelist_term_id varchar [note: 'Reference to datamanagement.codelist_term.codelist_term_id.']
  arm_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to study.study_arm. Business justification: SDTM DM domain requires ARM and ACTARM derivation from the authoritative study_arm definition. Baseline characteristic tables in CSR are stratified by arm.']
  consent_subject_consent_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to consent.subject_consent. Business justification: SDTM DM domain derivation requires the authoritative consent record to populate RFICDTC (informed consent date).']
  corrected_demographic_id varchar [note: 'Self-referencing FK on demographic (corrected_demographic_id)']
  enrollment_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to subject.enrollment. Business justification: Demographic records in clinical trials are captured per enrollment (SDTM DM domain is study-specific).']
  ethnicity_codelist_term_id varchar [note: 'Reference to datamanagement.codelist_term.codelist_term_id.']
  race_codelist_term_id varchar [note: 'Reference to datamanagement.codelist_term.codelist_term_id.']
  randomization_treatment_arm_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to randomization.treatment_arm. Business justification: SDTM DM domain requires ARM and ACTARM per subject derived from the canonical treatment_arm definition.']
  sex_codelist_term_id varchar [note: 'Reference to datamanagement.codelist_term.codelist_term_id.']
  study_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the clinical study for which this demographic record was collected. Links the subject demographics to the parent study context.']
  study_site_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the investigational site where the subject was enrolled and demographic data was collected.']
  trial_subject_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the trial subject (participant) whose demographic data is captured in this record. Core linkage to the trial_subject master entity.']
  age_at_screening varchar [note: 'Subject\'s age in whole years at the time of the screening visit, derived from date of birth and screening date. Used for eligibility verification, stratification, and CDISC SDTM DM domain submission.']
  birth_year varchar [note: 'Subject\'s year of birth as a four-digit integer. Used when full date of birth is masked for privacy compliance but year-level granularity is required for age-cohort analyses and CDISC partial date handling.']
  bmi decimal(5,2) [note: 'Subject\'s body mass index calculated as weight (kg) divided by height squared (m²) at baseline. Stored as a baseline characteristic per CDISC ADaM ADSL convention; used in eligibility assessment and subgroup analyses.']
  comments varchar [note: 'Free-text field for additional notes or clarifications related to the subject\'s demographic data, such as explanations for partial dates, data corrections, or special circumstances noted by the site or data manager.']
  country varchar [note: 'ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 three-letter country code representing the country where the subject was enrolled. Used for geographic subgroup analyses, regulatory reporting by region, and CDISC SDTM DM domain.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when the demographic record was first created in the silver layer lakehouse, in ISO 8601 format with timezone offset. Supports audit trail and data lineage requirements per 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+.']
  data_entry_status varchar [note: 'Current data entry and verification status of the demographic eCRF form in the EDC system. Tracks completeness and readiness for database lock (DBL) and SDTM submission.']
  data_source_system varchar [note: 'Identifies the operational system of record from which the demographic data was sourced. Supports data lineage, reconciliation, and audit trail requirements across the lakehouse pipeline.']
  date_of_birth date [note: 'Subject\'s date of birth in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-dd). Used to calculate age at key study milestones and to verify age-based eligibility criteria. May be partially masked (year only) per privacy regulations.']
  dm_sequence_number varchar [note: 'Sequential record number within the DM domain for a given subject, per CDISC SDTM convention. Used to uniquely identify each demographic record when multiple records exist per subject (e.g., re-screening scenarios).']
  edc_subject_key varchar [note: 'Source system record key for the subject\'s demographic record in the EDC system (Medidata Rave). Enables traceability from the silver layer back to the source EDC record for SDV and audit purposes.']
  epoch varchar [note: 'The study epoch (e.g., SCREENING, TREATMENT, FOLLOW-UP) during which the demographic data was collected, per CDISC SDTM Trial Epochs dataset. Used for temporal context in multi-epoch study designs.']
  first_exposure_date date [note: 'Date of the subject\'s first exposure to the investigational product (IP). Defines the start of the treatment period and is the reference date for study day calculations in CDISC SDTM DM domain.']
  gender_identity varchar [note: 'Subject\'s self-reported gender identity, distinct from biological sex. Collected per evolving FDA guidance on inclusion of gender identity in clinical trials.']
  height_cm decimal(6,2) [note: 'Subject\'s height in centimeters measured at baseline/screening visit. Used for body surface area (BSA) calculations, dose determination, and baseline characteristic tables in the Clinical Study Report (CSR).']
  informed_consent_date date [note: 'Date on which the subject signed the informed consent form (ICF) prior to any study-related procedures. Anchors the CDISC SDTM DM.RFICDTC reference date and is required for regulatory compliance and ALCOA+ data integrity.']
  last_exposure_date date [note: 'Date of the subject\'s last exposure to the investigational product (IP). Used to define the end of the treatment period and calculate treatment duration for safety and efficacy analyses.']
  lock_status varchar [note: 'Lock status of the demographic eCRF record in the EDC system. LOCKED records cannot be modified without an audit-trailed unlock. FROZEN records are pending final database lock (DBL).']
  protocol_version varchar [note: 'Version of the study protocol in effect at the time the demographic data was collected. Ensures traceability of demographic assessments to the applicable protocol amendment.']
  query_open_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether one or more open data queries (discrepancies) exist against this demographic record in the EDC system. True = at least one unresolved query; False = no open queries. Used for data cleaning tracking.']
  race_other_description varchar [note: 'Free-text description of race when the subject selects \'OTHER\' or \'MULTIPLE\' as their racial category. Captures verbatim self-reported race for completeness in regulatory submissions.']
  reference_start_date date [note: 'The protocol-defined reference start date for the subject, used as the anchor for study day (STUDYDAY) calculations across all SDTM domains. May differ from first_exposure_date in some study designs (e.g., observational studies).']
  sdtm_domain varchar [note: 'CDISC SDTM domain code for this record. Always \'DM\' for demographic records. Included to support automated SDTM dataset generation and regulatory submission pipelines.']
  sdv_status varchar [note: 'Status of source data verification (SDV) for the demographic record, indicating whether the EDC data has been verified against source documents by the Clinical Research Associate (CRA) during site monitoring.']
  subject_number varchar [note: 'Site-assigned subject number used to identify the participant within the study site. Typically formatted as a numeric or alphanumeric code assigned at screening or enrollment.']
  unique_subject_identifier varchar [note: 'Globally unique identifier for the subject across the study, constructed per CDISC SDTM convention (typically STUDYID-SITEID-SUBJID). Used as the primary cross-domain linkage key in SDTM submissions.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent update to the demographic record in the silver layer lakehouse. Used for incremental data processing, change detection, and audit trail compliance.']
  weight_kg decimal(6,2) [note: 'Subject\'s body weight in kilograms measured at baseline/screening visit. Used for dose calculations, PK/PD modeling, BMI derivation, and baseline characteristic tables in the CSR.']

  Note: 'Captures subject demographic data including age, sex, race, ethnicity, height, weight, and other baseline characteristics collected at screening per CDISC DM domain standards.'
}

Table subject.medical_history {
  medical_history_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique surrogate identifier for each medical history record in the clinical trial system. Primary key for the medical_history data product.']

  trial_subject_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the trial subject (patient) whose medical history is recorded. Core linkage to the trial_subject master record.']
  visit_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to subject.subject_visit. Business justification: Medical history is collected during screening visits. medical_history carries a denormalized screening_visit_number (STRING) that should be normalized via FK to subject_visit.']
  ae_related_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this medical history condition has been associated with or contributed to an adverse event (AE) reported during the study. Supports integrated safety analysis.']

  condition_category varchar [note: 'High-level category classifying the type of medical history entry. Corresponds to SDTM MHCAT variable. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: MEDICAL HISTORY|SURGICAL HISTORY|FAMILY HISTORY|PSYCHIATRIC HISTORY|ALLERGY|OBSTETRIC HISTORY — promote to reference product]']

  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp when this medical history record was first created in the EDC system or lakehouse. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.']
  edc_record_reference varchar [note: 'The unique record identifier assigned by the EDC system (Medidata Rave) for this medical history entry. Used for source data verification (SDV) and data reconciliation.']
  eligibility_relevant_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this medical history condition is relevant to the study\'s inclusion/exclusion eligibility criteria. Used by the medical monitor and data management team to assess protocol compliance.']
  lock_status varchar [note: 'Data lock status of this medical history record in the EDC system. Locked records cannot be modified without an authorized unlock procedure, supporting database lock (DBL) integrity.']
  meddra_llt varchar [note: 'The MedDRA Lowest Level Term (LLT) that most closely maps to the verbatim condition text. Provides the most granular level of MedDRA coding hierarchy.']
  meddra_pt varchar [note: 'The MedDRA Preferred Term (PT) assigned to the verbatim medical history condition during medical coding. Used for standardized regulatory reporting and safety analysis.']
  meddra_soc varchar [note: 'The MedDRA System Organ Class (SOC) associated with the coded medical history condition. Used for aggregate safety reporting and tabulation by body system.']
  meddra_version varchar [note: 'The version of the MedDRA dictionary used to code this medical history condition (e.g., 26.0). Required for regulatory submissions to ensure reproducibility of coding.']
  mh_seq varchar [note: 'Sequential number identifying each medical history record for a given subject within a study. Corresponds to the SDTM MHSEQ variable used in regulatory submissions.']
  ongoing_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the medical history condition was ongoing at the time of the subject\'s screening or baseline assessment. True = condition is still active; False = condition has resolved. Corresponds to SDTM MHENRF or MHONGO.']
  onset_date date [note: 'The date on which the pre-existing medical condition first began or was first diagnosed. May be partial (year only or year-month) per CDISC partial date conventions. Corresponds to SDTM MHSTDTC.']
  pre_existing_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the condition was present prior to the subject\'s first dose of investigational product. Distinguishes pre-existing conditions from treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) in safety analysis.']
  protocol_version varchar [note: 'The version of the study protocol in effect at the time this medical history record was collected. Ensures traceability of data to the applicable protocol amendment.']
  query_open_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether there is at least one open data query (discrepancy) against this medical history record in the EDC system. Supports data cleaning and database lock readiness tracking.']
  resolution_date date [note: 'The date on which the pre-existing medical condition resolved or ended. Null if the condition is ongoing at the time of assessment. Corresponds to SDTM MHENDTC.']
  sdtm_domain varchar [note: 'The CDISC SDTM domain code for this record. For medical history records this is always \'MH\'. Used during SDTM dataset generation for regulatory submissions.']
  sdv_date date [note: 'The date on which source data verification was completed for this medical history record by the Clinical Research Associate (CRA).']
  sdv_status varchar [note: 'Status of source data verification for this medical history record. Indicates whether the CRA has verified the eCRF data against source documents at the investigational site.']
  severity varchar [note: 'Clinical severity grading of the pre-existing medical condition as assessed by the investigator. Supports safety profiling and eligibility assessment.']
  source_system_record_reference varchar [note: 'The native primary key or record identifier of this medical history entry in the originating source system (e.g., Medidata Rave record OID). Enables bidirectional traceability between the lakehouse and the EDC.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp when this medical history record was last modified in the EDC system or lakehouse. Required for audit trail compliance and change tracking per 21 CFR Part 11.']
  verbatim_term varchar [note: 'STRING']

  Note: 'Records subject medical history and pre-existing conditions collected during screening, coded to MedDRA terms, with onset dates, resolution status, and relevance to study eligibility.'

Table subject.concomitant_medication {

  comments varchar [note: 'Free-text comments or notes entered by the investigator, CRC, or data manager regarding this concomitant medication record. May include clarifications on dose changes, interruptions, or special circumstances not captured in structured fields.']
  concomitant_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the medication was taken concomitantly (during the study treatment period) as opposed to only in the pre-study period. Supports classification of medications as prior vs. concomitant per SDTM CM domain conventions.']
  concomitant_medication_category varchar [note: 'Sponsor-defined category grouping for the concomitant medication (e.g., PRIOR, CONCOMITANT, PROHIBITED, RESCUE). Corresponds to SDTM CMCAT. Used for protocol-specific medication classification and reporting.']
  data_entry_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this concomitant medication record was first entered into the EDC system (Medidata Rave). Supports ALCOA+ audit trail requirements and 21 CFR Part 11 electronic record compliance.']
  dose decimal(10,4) [note: 'The numeric dose amount of the concomitant medication administered per dose event. Corresponds to SDTM CMDOSE. Must be interpreted in conjunction with dose_unit.']
  dose_frequency varchar [note: 'The frequency at which the concomitant medication is administered (e.g., QD, BID, TID, QID, PRN, weekly). Corresponds to SDTM CMDOSFRQ. Uses CDISC controlled terminology for standardized reporting.']
  end_date date [note: 'The date on which the subject stopped taking the concomitant medication. Corresponds to SDTM CMENDTC (date portion). Null if medication is ongoing at time of data collection. Used for duration calculations and temporal overlap analysis.']
  indication varchar [note: 'The clinical reason or medical condition for which the concomitant medication is being taken, as reported by the subject or investigator. Corresponds to SDTM CMINDC. Used for safety and drug-drug interaction analysis.']
  last_modified_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this concomitant medication record was most recently modified in the source EDC system. Required for audit trail compliance per 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.']
  modified_drug_name varchar [note: 'Standardized or sponsor-modified version of the verbatim drug name after data cleaning, prior to WHO-DD coding. Corresponds to SDTM CMMODIFY. Used when the verbatim term is modified for coding purposes.']
  ongoing_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the concomitant medication was still ongoing at the time of the last assessment or data collection. Corresponds to SDTM CMONGO. True when end_date is not yet known or medication continues beyond the observation window.']
  prior_therapy_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the medication was taken prior to the start of the study (pre-existing medication) as opposed to being initiated during the study. Corresponds to SDTM CMPRESP/CMOCCUR context.']
  prohibited_medication_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this concomitant medication is classified as a prohibited medication per the study protocol. A True value may trigger a protocol deviation review. Critical for protocol compliance monitoring.']
  query_open_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether there is at least one open data discrepancy query against this concomitant medication record in the EDC system. Supports data management workflow tracking and database lock (DBL) readiness assessment.']
  record_status varchar [note: 'Current data management status of the concomitant medication record in the EDC system (Medidata Rave). Indicates whether the record is active, has been deleted, amended after lock, or locked for database lock (DBL).']
  rescue_medication_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this medication was administered as a rescue therapy per the study protocol (e.g., for breakthrough pain, hypoglycemia rescue). Rescue medication use is a key efficacy endpoint in many trials.']
  sdtm_domain varchar [note: 'The CDISC SDTM domain code for this record. Always \'CM\' (Concomitant and Prior Medications) for records in this product. Used for SDTM dataset generation and regulatory submission via eCTD.']
  sdv_status varchar [note: 'Current source data verification (SDV) status for this concomitant medication record, as tracked by the Clinical Research Associate (CRA) in the CTMS. Indicates whether the data has been verified against source documents.']
  source_record_reference varchar [note: 'The native record identifier from the source EDC system (e.g., Medidata Rave internal record key) for this concomitant medication entry. Enables bidirectional traceability between the lakehouse Silver Layer and the operational system of record.']
  start_date date [note: 'The date on which the subject began taking the concomitant medication. Corresponds to SDTM CMSTDTC (date portion). Used to determine temporal overlap with investigational product exposure and adverse event onset.']
  study_day_end varchar [note: 'The study day on which the concomitant medication was stopped, calculated relative to the reference start date. Corresponds to SDTM CMENDY. Null if medication is ongoing. Used for duration and overlap calculations.']
  study_day_start varchar [note: 'The study day on which the concomitant medication was started, calculated relative to the reference start date (Day 1 = first dose of investigational product). Corresponds to SDTM CMSTDY. Enables temporal analysis relative to IP exposure.']
  subcategory varchar [note: 'Sponsor-defined subcategory for further classification of the concomitant medication within its category (e.g., ANALGESIC, ANTIBIOTIC, ANTIHYPERTENSIVE). Corresponds to SDTM CMSCAT. Enables granular therapeutic class reporting.']
  verbatim_drug_name varchar [note: 'The medication name exactly as reported by the subject or investigator on the electronic Case Report Form (eCRF), prior to WHO-DD coding. Corresponds to SDTM CMTRT field. Preserved for source data traceability per ALCOA+ principles.']
  verbatim_term varchar [note: 'STRING']
  whodrug_atc_code varchar [note: 'The Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical (ATC) classification code assigned by the WHO Drug Dictionary (WHO-DD) for the concomitant medication. Enables therapeutic class-level analysis and drug-drug interaction assessment.']
  whodrug_drug_name varchar [note: 'WHODrug drug name (verbatim/coded).']
  whodrug_version varchar [note: 'Version of the WHO Drug Dictionary (WHO-DD) used for coding this concomitant medication record. Required for regulatory submissions to ensure reproducibility of coded data.']

  Note: 'Records medications taken by subjects before and during the trial, including drug name, indication, dose, route, start/stop dates, and WHO-DD coding.'
}

  Note: 'This association product represents the Informed Consent Event between a trial_subject and a document_icf_version. It captures the complete regulatory audit trail of every consent and re-consent signing event for each subject across all ICF versions'

  medical_history_related boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the adverse event is considered related to or a continuation of a pre-existing medical history condition, as assessed by the investigator. Supports pre-existing condition confounding analysis.']

  report_type varchar [note: 'Indicates whether this record represents the initial AE report, a follow-up update with new clinical information, or the final report upon event resolution. Supports version history tracking as the clinical picture evolves.']

  seriousness_criteria varchar [note: 'Specific ICH E2A seriousness criterion or criteria met by this SAE (e.g., death, life-threatening, hospitalization required, persistent disability, congenital anomaly, medically significant). Multiple criteria may apply.']
  severity varchar [note: 'Severity or intensity of adverse event (verbatim/submission value); see severity_ct_term_id for controlled terminology reference']
  study_day_onset varchar [note: 'The study day (relative to first dose date) on which the adverse event began. Calculated per CDISC convention (Day 1 = first dose date). Used in time-to-event analyses and safety exposure-adjusted incidence calculations.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp when this adverse event record was most recently modified in the source system. Supports change tracking, audit trail compliance, and incremental data loading in the Databricks Silver layer.']

  verbatim_term_ae varchar [note: 'description']
  version_number varchar [note: 'Sequential version number of this AE record, incremented with each follow-up update. Version 1 is the initial report; subsequent versions capture evolving clinical information. Enables temporal evolution tracking across the AE lifecycle.']

  Note: 'Core master record for every adverse event (AE) reported during a clinical trial, capturing onset date, resolution date, severity grade per CTCAE, seriousness flag, expectedness, relationship to investigational product, action taken, outcome, and'

  lab_result_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to laboratory.laboratory_lab_result. Business justification: SAE expedited reports (CIOMS/MedWatch, ICH E2B) require direct reference to the lab result that triggered or supported the SAE determination (e.g., elevated ALT for']
  manufacture_batch_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to supply.manufacture_batch. Business justification: SAE regulatory expedited reports (ICH E2A/E2B) require the specific IMP batch number for batch recall decisions and health authority submissions.']
  protocol_deviation_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to compliance.protocol_deviation. Business justification: Regulatory agencies (FDA, EMA) require SAE narratives to document whether a protocol deviation contributed to the SAE.']
  protocol_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to study.protocol. Business justification: SAE expectedness assessment and 7/15-day reporting timelines are protocol-version-specific. Regulatory SAE submissions to FDA/EMA require the protocol version.']
  study_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the clinical study (protocol) under which the SAE occurred. Used for regulatory reporting and safety signal aggregation across the study.']
  study_site_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to site.study_site. Business justification: SAE aggregate reporting and site risk tiering require linking SAEs to the study_site record, which holds per-protocol SAE counts, monitoring visit data, and risk tier.']
  subject_randomization_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to randomization.subject_randomization. Business justification: SAE regulatory submissions (CIOMS I, MedWatch) require the subject\'s treatment arm from the authoritative randomization record.']
  subject_visit_data_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to datamanagement.subject_visit_data. Business justification: SAE data is captured via eCRF at a specific subject visit; safety data managers reconcile SAE source data against subject_visit_data records during DBL and regulatory']
  submission_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to regulatory.submission. Business justification: SAEs meeting expedited reporting criteria (7-day/15-day) are packaged into regulatory submissions.']
  tmf_document_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to document.tmf_document. Business justification: SAE reports are ICH E6 GCP essential documents that must be filed in the TMF. Regulatory inspectors verify SAE documentation in the TMF.']
  trial_subject_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the study subject (patient/participant) who experienced the SAE. Serves as the PARTY_REFERENCE for this transaction header per canonical attribute rules.']
  withdrawal_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to consent.withdrawal. Business justification: SAEs frequently cause subject withdrawal. The SAE record must reference the withdrawal for complete case documentation, CSR subject disposition tables, and regulatory submissions requiring']
  action_taken varchar [note: 'The action taken with the investigational product in response to the SAE (e.g., dose reduced, drug withdrawn, dose interrupted). This is a key regulatory field in ICSR submissions and clinical study reports.']
  argus_case_number varchar [note: 'Externally-known unique case identifier assigned by the source system upon SAE intake. This is the BUSINESS_IDENTIFIER used for cross-system traceability, regulatory submissions, and sponsor communications.']
  blinding_status varchar [note: 'Indicates whether the SAE case is currently blinded (treatment assignment unknown) or unblinded (treatment assignment revealed for safety reporting purposes). Unblinding may be required for SUSAR reporting to regulatory authorities.']
  causality_assessment varchar [note: 'The investigator\'s assessment of the causal relationship between the investigational product and the SAE. This is a critical regulatory field used to determine whether the event qualifies as a Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction (SUSAR).']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp when the SAE record was first created in the source system Serves as the RECORD_AUDIT_CREATED field per canonical transaction header requirements. Conforms to 21 CFR Part 11 audit trail requirements.']
  ctcae_grade varchar [note: 'The CTCAE severity grade assigned to the SAE, ranging from 1 (mild) to 5 (death). Grade 3 = severe, Grade 4 = life-threatening, Grade 5 = death. Used for oncology and other therapeutic area safety assessments.']
  dsmb_reported boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this SAE was reported to the Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) or Data Monitoring Committee (DMC) for independent safety review. Required for studies with an active DSMB/DMC charter.']
  expectedness varchar [note: 'Indicates whether the SAE is expected (listed in the Investigator\'s Brochure or product labeling) or unexpected (not listed or differing in nature/severity). Unexpected + serious + related = SUSAR, triggering expedited regulatory reporting.']
  follow_up_number varchar [note: 'Sequential number indicating which follow-up report this record represents (0 = initial report, 1 = first follow-up, 2 = second follow-up, etc.). Used to track the evolution of the SAE case over time as new information becomes available.']
  initial_report_date date [note: 'The date on which the SAE was first reported to the sponsor or CRO by the investigational site. This is Day 0 for calculating regulatory reporting timelines (e.g., 7-day or 15-day expedited reporting clock).']
  irb_iec_notification_date date [note: 'The date on which the Institutional Review Board (IRB) or Independent Ethics Committee (IEC) was notified of the SAE. Required under GCP and local regulations to ensure ongoing ethical oversight of the study.']
  is_susar boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this SAE has been classified as a Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction (SUSAR), requiring expedited regulatory reporting to health authorities (e.g., FDA 7/15-day reporting, EMA reporting).']
  narrative varchar [note: 'The full medical narrative describing the SAE, including clinical course, relevant medical history, concomitant medications, investigational product details, and the investigator\'s assessment.']
  onset_date date [note: 'The date on which the serious adverse event first began or was first observed by the subject or investigator. This is the principal BUSINESS_EVENT_TIMESTAMP (date precision) for the SAE transaction.']
  outcome varchar [note: 'The clinical outcome of the serious adverse event at the time of the most recent report. \'recovered_with_sequelae\' indicates the subject recovered but with lasting effects. \'fatal\' must align with seriousness_death = true.']
  regulatory_report_due_date date [note: 'The calculated deadline by which the expedited regulatory report (e.g., IND Safety Report, SUSAR notification) must be submitted to the relevant health authority.']
  report_type varchar [note: 'Classifies the type of safety report generated for this SAE. \'expedited\' = 7/15-day SUSAR or IND safety report; \'periodic\' = included in DSUR/PSUR; \'spontaneous\' = post-marketing spontaneous report; \'literature\' = identified from published literature.']
  reporting_authority varchar [note: 'The health authority or regulatory body to which the SAE/SUSAR report was submitted (e.g., \'FDA\', \'EMA\', \'MHRA\', \'PMDA\', \'TGA\', \'Health Canada\'). May contain multiple authorities if reported to more than one.']
  resolution_date date [note: 'The date on which the serious adverse event resolved, stabilized, or the subject died. Null if the event is ongoing at the time of reporting.']
  sae_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the SAE case in the source system \'initial\' = first report received; \'follow_up\' = additional information received; \'closed\' = case fully resolved and closed; \'nullified\' = case determined not to meet SAE criteria and voided.']
  sae_term varchar [note: 'The verbatim (as-reported) description of the serious adverse event as recorded by the investigator or site staff in the source document or eCRF. This is the raw, uncoded term prior to MedDRA coding.']
  seriousness_congenital_anomaly boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the SAE meets the regulatory seriousness criterion of resulting in a congenital anomaly or birth defect in the offspring of the subject.']
  seriousness_death boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the SAE meets the regulatory seriousness criterion of resulting in death of the subject. One of the six ICH E2A seriousness criteria that must be captured individually.']
  seriousness_disability boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the SAE meets the regulatory seriousness criterion of resulting in persistent or significant disability or incapacity.']
  seriousness_hospitalization boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the SAE meets the regulatory seriousness criterion of requiring inpatient hospitalization or prolongation of existing hospitalization.']
  seriousness_life_threatening boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the SAE meets the regulatory seriousness criterion of being immediately life-threatening (i.e., the subject was at immediate risk of death at the time of the event).']
  seriousness_medically_important boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the SAE meets the regulatory seriousness criterion of being an other medically important condition — events that may not be immediately life-threatening but may jeopardize the subject or require intervention to prevent one of the other']
  source_document_reference varchar [note: 'Reference identifier for the source document (e.g., hospital discharge summary, death certificate, medical records) that supports the SAE report. Used for SDV and audit trail purposes per ALCOA+ principles.']
  sponsor_receipt_date date [note: 'The date on which the sponsor (or CRO acting on behalf of the sponsor) received the complete minimum information required to process the SAE. This date starts the regulatory reporting clock per ICH E2A.']
  subject_number varchar [note: 'The protocol-assigned subject identifier (e.g., site-subject number) for the patient who experienced the SAE. Restricted as it can be used to identify an individual participant in combination with study data.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp when the SAE record was most recently modified in the source system Serves as the RECORD_AUDIT_UPDATED field per canonical transaction header requirements. Required for 21 CFR Part 11 audit trail compliance.']

  Note: 'Transactional record for Serious Adverse Events (SAEs) that meet regulatory seriousness criteria (death, life-threatening, hospitalization, disability, congenital anomaly, or other medically important condition).'
}

Table safety.susar {
