  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when this laboratory result record was first created in the data management system. Audit trail field required for 21 CFR Part 11 compliance and ALCOA+ data integrity principles.']
  critical_value_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this result meets the laboratory\'s critical (panic) value threshold requiring immediate clinical notification. True triggers safety review workflow and potential SAE/AE assessment per protocol.']
  data_origin varchar [note: 'Source system or method by which this laboratory result was entered into the data management system. EDC: entered via Medidata Rave eCRF; LAB_DIRECT: electronic lab data transfer; MANUAL: manual data entry; MIGRATION: legacy data migration; BIOANALYTICAL']
  dbl_included_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this result was included in the locked database at the time of Database Lock (DBL). False indicates the result was added or modified post-lock (requires formal database unlock procedure). Critical for regulatory submission integrity.']
  esource_capture_datetime timestamp [note: 'The esource capture datetime of the laboratory lab result.']
  esource_system_name varchar [note: 'The esource system name of the laboratory lab result.']
  esource_verified_flag boolean [note: 'Indicator for esource verified flag on the laboratory lab result.']
  fasting_status varchar [note: 'Fasting status; implements SDTM LB.LBFAST']
  fhir_resource_reference varchar [note: 'FHIR resource reference to source Observation; implements FHIR Reference.reference']
  fhir_resource_type varchar [note: 'FHIR resource type; implements FHIR Resource.resourceType']
  lbcat varchar [note: 'Lab category; implements SDTM LB.LBCAT']
  lbscat varchar [note: 'Lab subcategory; implements SDTM LB.LBSCAT']
  method varchar [note: 'Test method; implements SDTM LB.LBMETHOD']
  normal_range_lower decimal(18,6) [note: 'Reference range lower limit; implements SDTM LB.LBORNRLO']
  normal_range_upper decimal(18,6) [note: 'Reference range upper limit; implements SDTM LB.LBORNRHI']
  out_of_range_flag boolean [note: 'Out-of-range indicator; implements SDTM LB.LBNRIND']
  query_open_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether there is at least one open data query (discrepancy) associated with this laboratory result in the EDC system (Medidata Rave). Supports data management workflow and DBL readiness tracking.']
  result_comment varchar [note: 'Free-text comment from the laboratory or data manager regarding this result (e.g., hemolyzed sample, lipemic specimen, instrument flag, repeat analysis note). Supports data review and query resolution.']
  result_received_datetime timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the laboratory result was received by the sponsor/CRO data management system (EDC or CTMS). Used for turnaround time monitoring and critical value notification tracking.']
  result_reported_datetime timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the laboratory formally reported and released the result. Distinct from collection and receipt timestamps. Used for lab turnaround time KPI calculation and audit trail.']
  result_seq_num varchar [note: 'Sequential number identifying the order of this result record within the subject\'s laboratory data. Maps to CDISC SDTM LBSEQ variable for dataset generation.']
  result_standard_unit varchar [note: 'Standardized unit; implements SDTM LB.LBSTRESU (CDISC CT UNIT codelist)']
  result_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the laboratory result indicating its data quality and review state. PRELIMINARY: initial unverified result; FINAL: verified and released; CORRECTED: amended after final release; CANCELLED: voided result; AMENDED: modified with']
  result_unit varchar [note: 'Original result unit; implements SDTM LB.LBORRESU (CDISC CT UNIT codelist)']
  result_value decimal(18,2) [note: 'Original result value; implements SDTM LB.LBORRES']
  result_value_numeric decimal(18,6) [note: 'Standardized numeric result; implements SDTM LB.LBSTRESN']
  sdv_status varchar [note: 'Status of source data verification (SDV) for this laboratory result, performed by the Clinical Research Associate (CRA) against source documents. Supports risk-based monitoring and GCP compliance.']
  source_fhir_resource varchar [note: 'Source eSource FHIR resource; implements FHIR Observation']
  source_system_code varchar [note: 'Foreign key to the source system reference that supplied this record']
  study_day varchar [note: 'Study day of collection; implements SDTM LB.LBDY']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when this laboratory result record was last modified. Audit trail field required for 21 CFR Part 11 compliance. Tracks corrections, amendments, and status changes throughout the data lifecycle.']
  usubjid varchar [note: 'Globally unique subject identifier in the format STUDYID-SITEID-SUBJID, as defined by CDISC SDTM. Required for regulatory submission datasets and cross-study subject traceability.']

  Note: 'Transactional record of a laboratory test result for a specific analyte from a subject specimen. Captures analyte name, LOINC code, result value, result unit, normal range lower/upper bound, reference range source, result status'
}

Table laboratory.specimen_collection {
  specimen_collection_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique surrogate identifier for each specimen collection event record in the clinical trial laboratory domain. Primary key for this transactional entity.']
  adverse_event_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to safety.adverse_event. Business justification: Unscheduled specimen collections are triggered by AEs (is_unscheduled flag exists). Linking specimen_collection to the triggering adverse_event supports AE-driven collection']
  arm_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to study.study_arm. Business justification: Safety and PD specimen collections are arm-specific in randomized trials. Arm-level collection compliance reporting, DSMB safety reviews, and SDTM LB domain generation require linking']
  compliance_sop_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to compliance.compliance_sop. Business justification: Specimen collection procedures (fasting verification, tube labeling, chain of custody initiation) are governed by compliance SOPs.']
  consent_subject_consent_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to consent.subject_consent. Business justification: GCP monitoring requires proof that each specimen collection event occurred under a valid, active informed consent.']
  ecrf_form_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the eCRF (Electronic Case Report Form) form in the EDC system (Medidata Rave) where this specimen collection event was recorded. Supports data lineage and source data verification (SDV).']
  epoch_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to study.epoch. Business justification: Specimen collections are epoch-specific for SDTM SC/LB domain mapping and safety monitoring. specimen_collection already has arm_id and study_visit_schedule_id but lacks epoch_id.']
  icf_version_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to consent.consent_icf_version. Business justification: GCP monitoring requires verification that each collection event was covered by the then-current IRB/IEC-approved ICF version.']
  investigational_site_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to site.investigational_site. Business justification: Specimens collected AT investigational sites require direct site context for collection logistics, site capabilities (has_local_laboratory), deviation tracking, and site contact']
  lab_facility_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to laboratory.lab_facility. Business justification: A specimen collection event is destined for a specific laboratory facility for analysis.']
  lab_kit_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to laboratory.lab_kit. Business justification: A specimen collection event uses a specific laboratory collection kit supplied to the site.']
  lab_panel_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the protocol-defined laboratory panel or test battery that this specimen collection is intended to fulfill.']
  protocol_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to study.protocol. Business justification: Specimen collections must be evaluated against the protocol version in effect at time of collection for protocol deviation assessment and regulatory audit.']
  protocol_lab_schedule_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to laboratory.protocol_lab_schedule. Business justification: A specimen collection event is the operational execution of a protocol-mandated lab assessment schedule.']
  regulatory_protocol_amendment_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to regulatory.regulatory_protocol_amendment. Business justification: Regulatory submissions must demonstrate that specimen collections were performed under the correct approved protocol version.']
  specimen_shipment_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to laboratory.specimen_shipment. Business justification: A specimen collection event results in specimens being shipped to the laboratory, and this shipment is tracked in specimen_shipment.']
  study_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the clinical study under which this specimen collection event occurred. Links the collection to the governing protocol.']
  study_site_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the clinical site (investigative site) where the specimen collection event took place.']
  study_visit_schedule_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to study.study_visit_schedule. Business justification: Specimen collections are planned against protocol-defined visit schedules. Linking actual collections to the scheduled visit definition enables visit-window deviation detection']
  subject_randomization_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to randomization.subject_randomization. Business justification: Specimen collection compliance requires confirming subject\'s randomization status and treatment arm at collection time — especially for PK/PD assessments where collection']
  trial_subject_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the trial subject (patient) from whom the specimen was collected. Core party reference for this transactional event.']
  visit_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the scheduled or unscheduled study visit during which the specimen was collected. Links collection to the visit schedule.']
  withdrawal_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to consent.withdrawal. Business justification: When a subject withdraws consent, specimen collections must be flagged, halted, or voided.']
  barcode varchar [note: 'Barcode or unique label identifier affixed to the specimen tube or container at the time of collection. Used for automated specimen tracking and laboratory information system (LIS) integration.']
  chain_of_custody_number varchar [note: 'Unique tracking number assigned to document the chain of custody for the specimen from collection through laboratory receipt. Ensures specimen integrity and traceability for regulatory and legal purposes.']
  collection_method varchar [note: 'The clinical method or procedure used to collect the specimen from the subject (e.g., venipuncture, fingerstick, lumbar puncture, biopsy). Corresponds to CDISC SDTM LBMETHOD.']
  collection_number varchar [note: 'Externally-known, human-readable business identifier for this specimen collection event, typically generated by the EDC or CTMS (e.g., \'SC-0042-001\'). Used for cross-system traceability and chain-of-custody documentation.']
  collection_site_anatomy varchar [note: 'The anatomical location on the subject\'s body from which the specimen was collected (e.g., \'Left Antecubital Vein\', \'Right Arm\', \'Lumbar Region\'). Corresponds to CDISC SDTM LBLOC.']
  collection_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the specimen collection event. Indicates whether the collection was completed as planned, partially completed, missed, or cancelled.']
  collection_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Specimen collection date/time; implements SDTM --DTC']
  collector_name varchar [note: 'Full name of the CRC or phlebotomist who performed the specimen collection. Denormalized for audit trail and regulatory inspection readiness. Classified as confidential as it identifies site personnel.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when this specimen collection record was first created in the system. Required for audit trail compliance under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.']
  deviation_description varchar [note: 'Free-text description of any deviation from the protocol-specified collection procedure, including wrong tube type, incorrect volume, missed time window, or improper storage. Populated when has_deviation = True.']
  deviation_type varchar [note: 'Categorical classification of the type of collection deviation observed. Used for trending and CAPA (Corrective and Preventive Action) analysis. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: timing|volume|tube_type|storage|labeling|processing|other — promote to reference product]']
  fasting_status varchar [note: 'Fasting status at collection; implements SDTM --FAST (CDISC CT NY codelist)']
  has_deviation boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a protocol deviation or collection irregularity was recorded for this specimen collection event. True = deviation present; False = no deviation. Triggers downstream deviation management workflow.']
  hemolysis_grade varchar [note: 'Visual or instrument-assessed grade of hemolysis (red blood cell rupture) in the collected blood specimen. Hemolysis can interfere with laboratory assay results and may require recollection.']
  is_unscheduled boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this specimen collection was an unscheduled (ad hoc) event not defined in the original study protocol visit schedule. True = unscheduled; False = protocol-scheduled.']
  lipemia_grade varchar [note: 'Visual or instrument-assessed grade of lipemia (excess lipids causing turbidity) in the collected specimen. Lipemia can interfere with photometric assay results.']
  nominal_time_point varchar [note: 'Protocol-defined nominal time point label for PK/PD sample collection (e.g., \'Pre-dose\', \'0.5h\', \'1h\', \'2h\', \'4h\', \'8h\', \'24h\'). Used to align actual collection times to protocol-scheduled PK sampling windows.']
  processing_completed_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time at which pre-analytical processing of the specimen was completed at the collection site (e.g., centrifugation, aliquoting). Used to calculate processing turnaround time and assess sample integrity.']
  recollection_reason varchar [note: 'Reason why a repeat specimen collection is required. Populated when recollection_required = True. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: insufficient_volume|hemolysis|lipemia|clotted|mislabeled|lost_in_transit|expired_kit|other — promote to reference product]']
  recollection_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a repeat specimen collection is required due to inadequate sample, collection deviation, or laboratory rejection. True = recollection needed; False = no recollection required.']
  sample_adequacy varchar [note: 'Assessment of whether the collected specimen volume and quality are sufficient to perform all protocol-required laboratory analyses. Determined at the time of collection or upon receipt at the laboratory.']
  scheduled_collection_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The protocol-defined date and time at which the specimen collection was planned to occur per the study visit schedule. Used to calculate collection timing deviations.']
  specimen_type varchar [note: 'Specimen type; implements SDTM --SPEC (CDISC CT SPECTYPE codelist)']
  storage_temperature_c decimal(5,1) [note: 'Temperature in degrees Celsius at which the specimen was stored at the collection site prior to shipment to the central laboratory. Deviations from protocol-specified storage conditions may compromise sample integrity.']
  time_from_dose_hours decimal(8,2) [note: 'Elapsed time in hours between the subject\'s most recent investigational product dose and the specimen collection. Critical for PK (Pharmacokinetics) and DMPK (Drug Metabolism and Pharmacokinetics) sample timing analysis.']
  tube_count varchar [note: 'The total number of tubes, vials, or containers collected during this specimen collection event. Used for chain-of-custody tracking and sample accountability.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when this specimen collection record was last modified. Required for audit trail compliance under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.']
  volume_collected_ml decimal(10,3) [note: 'Total volume of specimen collected from the subject, expressed in millilitres (mL). Critical for PK/PD studies and for verifying adequacy of sample for planned assays.']
  volume_unit varchar [note: 'Unit of measure for the volume collected. Typically mL for blood/urine, but may be µL for microsampling or g for tissue. Ensures unambiguous interpretation of volume_collected_ml.']

  Note: 'Transactional record of a scheduled or unscheduled specimen collection event at a clinical site or subject visit. Captures collection event date/time, study visit reference, protocol-scheduled vs.'
}

Table laboratory.specimen_shipment {
  specimen_shipment_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique surrogate identifier for the specimen shipment record in the lakehouse silver layer. Primary key for this transactional entity.']
  clinical_trial_authorization_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to regulatory.clinical_trial_authorization. Business justification: Cross-border specimen shipments require import/export permits authorized under the CTA.']
  document_sop_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to document.document_sop. Business justification: Specimen shipment operations are governed by SOPs covering chain of custody, temperature monitoring, dangerous goods handling, and courier procedures.']
  investigational_site_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to site.investigational_site. Business justification: Shipments originate FROM investigational sites, requiring site address, contact (site_email, phone_number), operational_status, and time_zone for logistics coordination.']
  lab_facility_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the destination central or reference laboratory facility receiving the shipment. Supports routing and receipt confirmation.']
  study_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the clinical study under which the specimens were collected and shipped. Links shipment to the sponsoring protocol.']
  study_site_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the clinical site (origin) from which the specimens were dispatched. Supports chain-of-custody traceability back to the collecting site.']
  study_visit_schedule_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to study.study_visit_schedule. Business justification: Specimen shipments are triggered by protocol-scheduled visits. Linking shipment to study_visit_schedule enables visit-level chain-of-custody tracking, shipment compliance']
  tmf_document_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to document.tmf_document. Business justification: International specimen shipments require import/export permits, dangerous goods declarations (UN3373), and customs documentation filed as TMF essential documents.']
  actual_receipt_date timestamp [note: 'Date and time at which the receiving laboratory confirmed physical receipt of the shipment. Used to calculate transit duration and assess specimen integrity against stability windows.']
  airbill_number varchar [note: 'Air waybill or bill of lading number issued by the carrier for international or air freight shipments. Required for customs clearance and IATA dangerous goods documentation.']
  collection_date date [note: 'Date on which the specimens included in this shipment were collected from study subjects. Used to calculate specimen age at receipt and assess stability compliance.']
  comments varchar [note: 'Free-text field for additional notes or observations recorded by site staff, courier, or laboratory personnel regarding the shipment (e.g., packaging condition on arrival, partial delivery notes).']
  courier_name varchar [note: 'Name of the logistics carrier or courier service responsible for transporting the shipment (e.g., World Courier, FedEx Clinical, Marken). Supports vendor performance tracking.']
  courier_service_level varchar [note: 'Service tier selected for the shipment (e.g., overnight, two-day, international priority). Determines expected transit time and cost classification.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time at which this specimen shipment record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail and data lineage requirements per 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.']
  customs_declaration_number varchar [note: 'Reference number of the customs or import/export declaration filed for international specimen shipments. Required for cross-border regulatory compliance and specimen release at destination.']
  destination_lab_code varchar [note: 'Alphanumeric code identifying the receiving central or reference laboratory. Denormalized for manifest documentation and rapid chain-of-custody reporting.']
  dry_ice_weight_kg decimal(6,3) [note: 'Weight of dry ice (in kilograms) included in the shipment package. Required for IATA dangerous goods declaration when dry ice is used as a refrigerant. Applicable only when temperature_condition = dry_ice.']
  excursion_duration_minutes varchar [note: 'Total duration in minutes during which the shipment temperature was outside the acceptable range. Used by the laboratory to assess specimen viability and document deviation impact.']
  excursion_max_temp_c decimal(5,2) [note: 'Highest temperature (in degrees Celsius) recorded by the temperature monitor/data logger during transit. Populated only when a temperature excursion is detected. Supports specimen impact assessment.']
  excursion_min_temp_c decimal(5,2) [note: 'Lowest temperature (in degrees Celsius) recorded by the temperature monitor/data logger during transit. Populated only when a temperature excursion is detected. Supports specimen impact assessment.']
  expected_arrival_date date [note: 'Planned date on which the shipment is expected to arrive at the destination laboratory, as agreed with the courier at time of dispatch. Used to trigger overdue alerts.']
  hazardous_material_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the shipment contains materials classified as hazardous (e.g., Category B biological substances, dry ice). True = hazardous declaration required; False = non-hazardous. Drives IATA dangerous goods documentation requirements.']
  import_permit_number varchar [note: 'Regulatory import permit or authorization number required for cross-border shipment of biological specimens in certain jurisdictions. Ensures compliance with national biosafety and import regulations.']
  lab_contact_name varchar [note: 'Name of the designated contact person at the receiving laboratory responsible for accepting and processing the shipment. Used for courier delivery confirmation and discrepancy resolution.']
  origin_site_number varchar [note: 'Sponsor-assigned or regulatory site number of the clinical site dispatching the specimens. Denormalized for chain-of-custody documentation and regulatory audit trail without requiring a join.']
  packaging_type varchar [note: 'Type of packaging used for the shipment, indicating the thermal protection and containment method. Relevant for regulatory compliance with IATA P650 and specimen integrity documentation.']
  protocol_visit_name varchar [note: 'Name or label of the study protocol visit (e.g., Day 1, Week 4, End of Treatment) associated with the specimen collection event. Supports SDTM domain mapping and visit-level reconciliation.']
  receipt_confirmed_by varchar [note: 'Name or user identifier of the laboratory staff member who confirmed receipt of the shipment. Part of the chain-of-custody audit trail per ALCOA+ principles.']
  received_specimen_count varchar [note: 'Actual number of specimens confirmed by the receiving laboratory upon opening the shipment. Compared against specimen_count to identify discrepancies or missing specimens.']
  rejection_reason varchar [note: 'Free-text description of the reason the shipment was rejected at the receiving laboratory (e.g., temperature excursion, broken specimens, incorrect labeling, missing manifest). Populated only when shipment_status = rejected.']
  shipment_date timestamp [note: 'Date and time at which the shipment was handed over to the courier at the originating clinical site. Principal business event timestamp for this transaction. Recorded in ISO 8601 format with timezone offset.']
  shipment_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of the specimen shipment. Drives chain-of-custody workflow and exception management. Values: pending (prepared, not yet dispatched), in_transit (with courier), delivered (courier confirmed delivery), received (lab confirmed']
  shipment_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the shipment by its clinical purpose. Values: routine (standard scheduled collection), urgent (expedited for safety or protocol reasons), pk_sample (Pharmacokinetics samples requiring strict timing), biomarker (exploratory biomarker']
  specimen_count varchar [note: 'Total number of individual specimen tubes, aliquots, or containers included in this shipment as declared on the manifest. Used for reconciliation at receipt.']
  subject_count varchar [note: 'Number of distinct study subjects whose specimens are included in this shipment. Supports subject-level reconciliation and enrollment tracking at the laboratory.']
  temperature_condition varchar [note: 'Required temperature storage and transport condition for the shipment as specified in the laboratory manual. Critical for specimen integrity. Values: ambient (15–25°C), refrigerated (2–8°C), frozen (-20°C), dry_ice (-78°C), liquid_nitrogen (-196°C).']
  temperature_excursion_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a temperature excursion (deviation outside the acceptable range) was detected during transit. True = excursion occurred; False = no excursion. Triggers specimen usability assessment workflow.']
  temperature_max_c decimal(5,2) [note: 'Upper bound of the acceptable temperature range (in degrees Celsius) for this shipment as defined in the study laboratory manual. Used to evaluate temperature excursion severity.']
  temperature_min_c decimal(5,2) [note: 'Lower bound of the acceptable temperature range (in degrees Celsius) for this shipment as defined in the study laboratory manual. Used to evaluate temperature excursion severity.']
  temperature_monitor_code varchar [note: 'Serial number or identifier of the temperature data logger or indicator device placed in the shipment. Enables retrieval of the full temperature log for excursion investigation and regulatory documentation.']
  temperature_monitor_type varchar [note: 'Type of temperature monitoring device included in the shipment. Data_logger provides continuous electronic recording; indicator_card provides a visual pass/fail indicator; none indicates no monitoring device was used.']
  tracking_number varchar [note: 'Carrier-assigned tracking number for the shipment package, enabling real-time logistics monitoring and proof-of-delivery confirmation.']
  un_number varchar [note: 'United Nations dangerous goods classification number for the shipment contents (e.g., UN3373 for Category B biological substances, UN1845 for dry ice). Required on shipping labels and documentation when hazardous_material_flag is True.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time at which this specimen shipment record was most recently modified. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and incremental ETL processing in the Databricks lakehouse.']

  Note: 'Transactional record tracking the shipment of specimens from a clinical site to a central or reference laboratory. Captures shipment manifest ID, origin site, destination lab facility, courier name, tracking number, shipment date/time, expected arrival'
}

Table laboratory.reference_range {
  reference_range_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique surrogate identifier for each reference range record in the laboratory master. Primary key for the reference_range data product.']
  arm_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to study.arm. Business justification: Reference ranges can be arm-specific (e.g., different normal ranges for dose-escalation vs. control arms).']
  bioanalytical_assay_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to laboratory.bioanalytical_assay. Business justification: A reference range (normal range) for a bioanalytical analyte is defined in the context of a specific validated bioanalytical assay — the LLOQ, ULOQ, and normal ranges are']
  compliance_sop_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to compliance.compliance_sop. Business justification: Reference range approval and change control are governed by compliance SOPs (ICH E3, CDISC CDASH).']
  epoch_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to study.epoch. Business justification: Reference ranges differ by epoch (baseline vs. treatment vs. follow-up). Epoch-specific ranges are required for SDTM LB domain LBNRIND derivation and DSMB safety reports.']
  lab_facility_id varchar [note: 'Identifier of the central or local laboratory facility that owns and applies this reference range. Links to the lab facility master.']
  lab_panel_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to laboratory.lab_panel. Business justification: Reference ranges are often defined in the context of a specific lab panel (e.g., a chemistry panel has specific normal ranges for its analytes).']
  protocol_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to study.protocol. Business justification: Sponsor-defined reference ranges are specified per protocol version for SDTM/ADaM dataset generation.']
  sap_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to biostatistics.the source system. Business justification: FDA/EMA submissions require that reference ranges used for out-of-range flagging and CTCAE grading match those specified in the the source system.']
  study_id varchar [note: 'Identifier of the clinical study for which this reference range is specifically applicable. Null indicates a lab-standard range applicable across all studies at the facility.']
  treatment_arm_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to randomization.treatment_arm. Business justification: In oncology and dose-escalation trials, reference ranges are arm-specific (e.g., different toxicity thresholds per dose level).']
  age_max decimal(5,2) [note: 'Maximum age in years of the subject population for which this reference range applies. Null indicates no upper age bound.']
  age_min decimal(5,2) [note: 'Minimum age in years of the subject population for which this reference range applies. Used to stratify ranges by pediatric, adult, or geriatric populations.']
  age_unit varchar [note: 'Unit of measurement for the age range fields (age_min, age_max). Defaults to years for adults; may be months, weeks, or days for neonatal or pediatric populations.']
  approval_status varchar [note: 'Current approval lifecycle status of this reference range version. Only approved ranges are used for out-of-range flagging and CTCAE grading in clinical trial lab results.']
  approved_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when this reference range version was formally approved by the authorized laboratory or sponsor personnel. Part of the GCP-required audit trail.']
  change_reason varchar [note: 'Coded reason explaining why this reference range version was created or updated. Required for GCP audit trail. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE']
  change_reason_detail varchar [note: 'Free-text narrative providing additional detail on the reason for the reference range update. Supplements the coded change_reason field for regulatory audit trail documentation.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when this reference range record was first created in the system. Part of the mandatory GCP audit trail for laboratory data per ALCOA+ principles.']
  critical_high decimal(18,6) [note: 'The critical (panic) high threshold for the analyte. Results at or above this value require immediate clinical notification per laboratory SOP and GCP safety reporting requirements.']
  critical_low decimal(18,6) [note: 'The critical (panic) low threshold for the analyte. Results at or below this value require immediate clinical notification per laboratory SOP and GCP safety reporting requirements.']
  ctcae_grade1_upper decimal(18,6) [note: 'Upper boundary value corresponding to CTCAE Grade 1 toxicity for this analyte. Used for automated CTCAE grading of laboratory results in safety and adverse event reporting.']
  ctcae_grade2_upper decimal(18,6) [note: 'Upper boundary value corresponding to CTCAE Grade 2 toxicity for this analyte. Used for automated CTCAE grading of laboratory results in safety and adverse event reporting.']
  ctcae_grade3_upper decimal(18,6) [note: 'Upper boundary value corresponding to CTCAE Grade 3 toxicity for this analyte. Used for automated CTCAE grading of laboratory results in safety and adverse event reporting.']
  ctcae_grade4_upper decimal(18,6) [note: 'Upper boundary value corresponding to CTCAE Grade 4 toxicity for this analyte. Used for automated CTCAE grading of laboratory results in safety and adverse event reporting.']
  ctcae_version varchar [note: 'CTCAE version; implements CTCAE version metadata']
  effective_end_date date [note: 'Date on which this reference range version ceased to be effective. Null indicates the range is currently active. Populated when a new version supersedes this record.']
  effective_start_date date [note: 'Date from which this reference range version became or becomes effective for use in clinical trial lab result evaluation and out-of-range flagging.']
  ethnicity_applicability varchar [note: 'Ethnic or racial population for which this reference range is specifically calibrated (e.g., ALL for universal, or specific population codes per CDISC). Null or ALL indicates the range applies universally regardless of ethnicity.']
  instrument_code varchar [note: 'Identifier of the specific laboratory instrument or analyzer for which this reference range was established. Instrument-specific ranges are required when different analyzers produce systematically different results.']
  is_current_version boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this record represents the currently active version of the reference range for the given analyte, lab, and stratification combination. True = current; False = historical version.']
  is_sponsor_defined boolean [note: 'Boolean flag indicating whether this reference range was explicitly defined or mandated by the clinical trial sponsor, as opposed to being the laboratory\'s standard range. Sponsor-defined ranges take precedence for trial-specific out-of-range flagging.']
  lab_accreditation_standard varchar [note: 'Accreditation standard under which the laboratory facility that established this reference range is certified (e.g., CAP, CLIA, ISO 15189). Relevant for regulatory submissions and sponsor qualification of central labs.']
  loinc_code varchar [note: 'LOINC code of the analyte; implements LOINC code']
  lower_limit decimal(18,6) [note: 'The lower boundary of the normal reference range for the analyte. Values below this threshold are flagged as abnormally low. Corresponds to LBORNRLO in CDISC SDTM.']
  method_code varchar [note: 'Code identifying the analytical method or instrument platform used to generate results evaluated against this reference range (e.g., colorimetric, immunoassay, HPLC). Reference ranges may differ by method.']
  modified_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when this reference range record was last modified. Part of the mandatory GCP audit trail for laboratory data per ALCOA+ principles.']
  prior_lower_limit decimal(18,6) [note: 'The lower normal limit value from the immediately preceding version of this reference range. Retained for audit trail and regulatory inspection readiness per GCP requirements.']
  prior_upper_limit decimal(18,6) [note: 'The upper normal limit value from the immediately preceding version of this reference range. Retained for audit trail and regulatory inspection readiness per GCP requirements.']
  range_source varchar [note: 'Indicates whether this reference range is sponsor-defined (provided by the clinical trial sponsor), lab-standard (established by the laboratory facility), derived from a regulatory guideline, or from published literature.']
  reagent_lot_number varchar [note: 'Lot number of the reagent kit or calibrator associated with this reference range version. Captured when a reagent lot change triggers a reference range update per laboratory SOPs.']
  sex_applicability varchar [note: 'Sex applicability; implements SDTM SEX (CDISC CT SEX codelist)']
  specimen_type varchar [note: 'Type of biological specimen for which this reference range is applicable (e.g., serum, plasma, whole blood, urine). Corresponds to LBSPEC in CDISC SDTM. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: serum|plasma|whole_blood|urine|csf|tissue|saliva|other — promote to reference']
  unit_of_measure varchar [note: 'Unit of measure; implements CDISC CT UNIT codelist']
  upper_limit decimal(18,6) [note: 'The upper boundary of the normal reference range for the analyte. Values above this threshold are flagged as abnormally high. Corresponds to LBORNRHI in CDISC SDTM.']
  version_number varchar [note: 'Sequential integer version number of this reference range definition. Incremented each time the range is updated. Supports full version history and audit trail per GCP requirements.']

  Note: 'Master definition of laboratory reference ranges (normal ranges) for analytes, with full version history. Captures analyte/LOINC code, lower and upper normal limits, unit of measure, sex, age range, ethnicity applicability, specimen type, lab facility'
}

  actual_time_post_dose_hours decimal(10,4) [note: 'Calculated elapsed time in hours between the actual dose administration time and the actual sample collection time. Distinct from nominal_time_hours; used as the primary time variable in PK concentration-time profiles and non-compartmental analysis (NCA).']

  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time this PK sample record was first created in the source system (EDC or LIMS). Required for audit trail compliance under 21 CFR Part 11 and ICH E6(R2). Represents the ALCOA+ \'contemporaneous\' requirement.']
  dose_administration_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The actual date and time of the reference dose administration used to calculate actual time post-dose for this sample. Sourced from the dosing record in the EDC (Medidata Rave). Required for accurate ATPT calculation per CDISC SDTM PC domain conventions.']
  dose_number varchar [note: 'The sequential dose number relative to which this PK sample was collected (e.g., 1 for first dose, steady-state dose number). Critical for distinguishing single-dose PK from multiple-dose/steady-state PK profiles in DMPK analysis.']
  edc_form_reference varchar [note: 'The reference identifier of the eCRF form in the EDC system (Medidata Rave) where this PK sample collection event was recorded. Enables direct traceability from the silver-layer data product back to the source EDC record for SDV and audit purposes.']
  exclusion_reason varchar [note: 'Free-text or coded reason for excluding this PK sample from the primary analysis dataset. Populated only when sample_exclusion_flag is True. Examples include \'Outside sampling window\', \'Haemolysed sample\', \'Vomiting within 2h of dose\', \'Bioanalytical']
  freeze_thaw_cycles varchar [note: 'The number of freeze-thaw cycles the PK sample has undergone. Excessive freeze-thaw cycles can degrade analyte stability and invalidate bioanalytical results.']

  nominal_time_hours decimal(10,4) [note: 'Numeric representation of the nominal time point in hours relative to dose administration (e.g., -0.0833 for pre-dose, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0). Negative values indicate pre-dose collections.']

  pre_dose_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this sample is a pre-dose (trough/baseline) collection. True = pre-dose sample; False = post-dose sample. Pre-dose samples are used to assess trough concentrations, baseline drug levels, and accumulation ratios in multiple-dose PK']

  processing_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time the sample was processed (e.g., centrifuged and aliquoted) after collection. Time from collection to processing is a critical pre-analytical variable that can affect analyte stability and bioanalytical results.']
  protocol_deviation_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a protocol deviation was associated with this PK sample collection event (e.g., collection outside the acceptable sampling window, incorrect tube used, missed collection). True = deviation present; False = no deviation.']
  sample_code varchar [note: 'Externally-known, human-readable unique identifier for the PK sample, typically printed on the sample tube label and used across CTMS, LIMS, and bioanalytical systems for chain-of-custody tracking. Corresponds to the specimen barcode or accession number.']
  sample_condition_on_receipt varchar [note: 'Assessment of the physical condition of the PK sample upon receipt at the bioanalytical laboratory. Conditions such as haemolysis, lipaemia, or temperature excursion may affect analyte measurement and trigger sample rejection or result flagging.']
  sample_exclusion_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this PK sample has been excluded from the primary PK analysis dataset. True = excluded; False = included. Exclusions may be due to protocol deviations, sample integrity issues, or bioanalytical failures.']
  sample_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the PK sample from scheduled collection through bioanalytical reporting. Drives workflow routing in LIMS and CTMS. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE']
  sample_type varchar [note: 'The biological matrix type of the PK sample. Determines the bioanalytical method applied and the reference range for analyte concentration. Plasma and serum are most common for small molecule PK; urine for renal clearance studies; CSF for CNS penetration']
  sampling_window_end_hours decimal(8,4) [note: 'The protocol-defined acceptable latest collection time in hours relative to dose for this nominal time point. Together with sampling_window_start_hours, defines the acceptable window for protocol compliance assessment.']
  sampling_window_start_hours decimal(8,4) [note: 'The protocol-defined acceptable earliest collection time in hours relative to dose for this nominal time point. Used to assess whether the actual collection time falls within the acceptable PK sampling window for protocol compliance determination.']
  sdtm_domain varchar [note: 'Target SDTM domain (PC/PP); implements SDTM Dataset.DOMAIN']
  storage_temperature_c decimal(6,2) [note: 'The temperature in degrees Celsius at which the PK sample is stored prior to shipment or analysis. Critical for analyte stability monitoring; deviations from protocol-specified storage conditions (e.g., -70°C, -20°C) must be documented and assessed for']
  subject_number varchar [note: 'The protocol-assigned subject number (e.g., site-subject identifier such as 001-001) used to identify the participant in regulatory submissions and PK analysis datasets.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time this PK sample record was most recently modified. Required for audit trail and data integrity monitoring under 21 CFR Part 11 and ICH E6(R2). Used to detect unauthorized or unexplained data changes.']
  volume_collected_ml decimal(8,3) [note: 'The actual volume of biological sample collected from the subject, expressed in millilitres. Used for sample sufficiency assessment, bioanalytical aliquoting planning, and protocol compliance verification against the required volume specified in the PK']
  volume_required_ml decimal(8,3) [note: 'The protocol-specified minimum volume of sample required for the PK assay at this time point, expressed in millilitres. Used to assess whether the collected volume meets protocol requirements and to flag insufficient sample events.']
  within_sampling_window boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the actual sample collection time falls within the protocol-defined acceptable PK sampling window for this nominal time point. True = within window (compliant); False = outside window (potential protocol deviation).']

  Note: 'Master record for pharmacokinetic (PK) and pharmacodynamic (PD) samples collected per the study PK sampling schedule. Captures nominal and actual collection time relative to dose (pre-dose, post-dose hours), dose number, PK sampling window compliance'

  assay_name varchar [note: 'Full descriptive name of the bioanalytical assay as used in study protocols, validation reports, and regulatory submissions (e.g., \'LC-MS/MS Assay for Compound XYZ in Human Plasma\'). Satisfies MASTER_RESOURCE IDENTITY_LABEL category.']

  calibration_curve_model varchar [note: 'Mathematical regression model used to fit the calibration curve for back-calculation of analyte concentrations from instrument response. Common models include Linear (1/x or 1/x² weighting), Quadratic, 4-Parameter Logistic (4PL), and 5-Parameter Logistic']

  glp_compliant boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the assay was validated and is performed under Good Laboratory Practice (GLP) regulations. GLP compliance is required for nonclinical safety studies submitted to regulatory agencies. True = GLP-compliant; False = non-GLP.']
  inter_run_precision_cv decimal(6,3) [note: 'Between-run precision expressed as percent coefficient of variation (%CV) across multiple analytical runs during validation. Regulatory acceptance criterion is typically ≤15% (%CV). Stored as the worst-case value across QC levels.']
  internal_standard varchar [note: 'Name or identifier of the internal standard (IS) used in the assay for quantification normalization (e.g., stable isotope-labeled analog, structural analog).']
  intra_run_precision_cv decimal(6,3) [note: 'Within-run precision expressed as percent coefficient of variation (%CV) at the QC concentration levels, as determined during validation. Regulatory acceptance criterion is typically ≤15% (%CV), or ≤20% at LLOQ.']
  lloq decimal(18,6) [note: 'Lower Limit of Quantification — the lowest analyte concentration that can be reliably quantified with acceptable accuracy and precision per the validated method. Expressed in the unit defined by lloq_uloq_unit.']
  lloq_uloq_unit varchar [note: 'Unit of measurement for the LLOQ and ULOQ values (e.g., \'ng/mL\', \'pg/mL\', \'µg/mL\', \'nM\'). Must be consistent with the unit reported in PK/PD concentration data submitted to regulatory agencies.']
  long_term_stability_days varchar [note: 'Number of days for which analyte stability in the biological matrix at long-term storage conditions (typically -20°C or -70°C) has been validated. Samples stored beyond this period require re-validation of stability before results can be reported.']
  matrix_effect_assessed boolean [note: 'Indicates whether matrix effect (ion suppression/enhancement for LC-MS/MS; non-specific binding for LBA) was formally evaluated during validation. True = matrix effect experiments conducted; False = not assessed.']
  matrix_type varchar [note: 'Specimen matrix type; implements SDTM PC.PCSPEC (CDISC CT SPECTYPE codelist)']
  parallelism_assessed boolean [note: 'Indicates whether parallelism (serial dilution of incurred samples producing results parallel to the calibration curve) was assessed. Relevant primarily for LBA and immunogenicity assays. True = parallelism assessed; False = not assessed.']
  reference_standard_lot varchar [note: 'Lot number of the certified reference standard used to prepare calibration standards and quality control (QC) samples. Traceability of the reference standard lot is required for regulatory submissions and audit purposes.']
  sample_volume_required_ul decimal(10,3) [note: 'Minimum volume of biological matrix (in microliters) required per sample aliquot for a single assay run. Used for specimen collection planning, biobank management, and feasibility assessment of retrospective analyses.']
  selectivity_assessed boolean [note: 'Indicates whether selectivity (absence of interference from endogenous matrix components) was formally assessed during validation. True = selectivity experiments conducted and documented; False = not assessed.']
  species varchar [note: 'Biological species for which the assay has been validated. Assays validated in human matrices may differ from those validated in preclinical animal species used in DMPK studies. Drives applicability to clinical vs. nonclinical programs.']
  sponsor_assay_code varchar [note: 'Sponsor-assigned identifier for the assay as referenced in the study protocol, the source system, or regulatory submission. May differ from the CRO\'s internal assay code. Required for cross-referencing sponsor documents with CRO laboratory records.']
  stability_freeze_thaw_cycles varchar [note: 'Number of freeze-thaw cycles for which analyte stability in the biological matrix has been validated. Samples subjected to more freeze-thaw cycles than validated must be flagged or excluded from analysis.']
  storage_condition varchar [note: 'Required storage temperature and conditions for samples analyzed by this assay (e.g., \'-70°C ± 10°C\', \'-20°C\', \'2–8°C\'). Defines the chain-of-custody storage requirement for clinical samples to maintain analyte integrity.']
  superseded_by_assay_code varchar [note: 'Assay code of the newer version that replaces this assay when it is retired or superseded. Supports version lineage tracking and ensures historical sample results can be linked to the correct assay version.']
  uloq decimal(18,6) [note: 'Upper Limit of Quantification — the highest analyte concentration that can be reliably quantified within the validated dynamic range. Samples above ULOQ must be diluted and re-assayed. Expressed in the unit defined by lloq_uloq_unit.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent modification to the bioanalytical assay record. Required for audit trail compliance under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ data integrity principles. Tracks when assay parameters, validation status, or metadata were last changed.']
  validation_date date [note: 'Date on which the bioanalytical method validation was formally completed and the validation report was approved. Marks the point from which the assay is considered fit for regulated use in clinical sample analysis.']
  validation_status varchar [note: 'Current regulatory validation tier of the assay. \'Validated\' indicates full GLP/GCP-compliant validation per FDA/EMA/ICH M10 guidelines; \'Qualified\' indicates fit-for-purpose qualification; \'Exploratory\' indicates early-phase research use only; \'In']
  version_number varchar [note: 'Version identifier of the assay method (e.g., \'v1.0\', \'v2.1\'). Incremented when the assay undergoes method changes requiring partial or full re-validation. Enables traceability of which assay version was used for each study\'s sample analysis.']
  weighting_factor varchar [note: 'Statistical weighting factor applied to the calibration curve regression to minimize heteroscedasticity (e.g., \'1/x\', \'1/x²\', \'none\'). Documented in the validation report and applied consistently during sample analysis.']

  Note: 'Master definition of a validated bioanalytical assay used to quantify drug concentrations, biomarkers, or immunogenicity in clinical trial samples. Captures assay name, analyte measured, assay type (LC-MS/MS, ELISA, ECL, PCR, flow cytometry), validation'
}

  calibration_curve_accepted boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the calibration curve for the analytical run met pre-defined acceptance criteria (e.g., ≥75% of calibrators within ±15% of nominal, ±20% at LLOQ). A failed calibration curve invalidates all results from the run.']
  categorical_result varchar [note: 'Qualitative or categorical result for assays that produce non-numeric outcomes (e.g., POSITIVE/NEGATIVE for immunogenicity, BELOW_LLOQ for concentrations below the lower limit of quantification). Null when numeric_result is populated.']
  collection_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the biological sample was collected from the subject. The principal real-world event time for this bioanalytical result record. Maps to PCDTC in CDISC SDTM PC domain. Conforms to ISO 8601 format.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this bioanalytical result record was first created in the system of record. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ data integrity principles.']
  dilution_factor decimal(10,4) [note: 'The dilution factor applied to the sample prior to analysis when the original concentration exceeded the ULOQ. The reported result incorporates this factor. Maps to PCDILIND/PCDILUTN in CDISC SDTM PC domain.']
  exclusion_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this result has been excluded from the primary PK/PD analysis dataset (e.g., due to protocol deviation, sample integrity issue, or statistical outlier determination per the Statistical Analysis Plan).']
  exclusion_reason varchar [note: 'Free-text or coded reason for excluding this result from the PK/PD analysis dataset. Required when exclusion_flag is true. Examples: \'Sample collected outside protocol window\', \'Hemolyzed sample\', \'Calibration curve failure\', \'Subject vomited within 2']
  freeze_thaw_cycles varchar [note: 'Number of freeze-thaw cycles the sample underwent prior to analysis. Stability data from method validation defines the maximum allowable cycles; exceedance may invalidate the result.']
  isr_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this sample was selected for Incurred Sample Reanalysis (ISR), a regulatory requirement to demonstrate reproducibility of results in authentic study samples. ISR is mandatory for pivotal PK studies submitted to FDA and EMA.']
  isr_result varchar [note: 'Outcome of the Incurred Sample Reanalysis (ISR) assessment. PASS indicates the original and repeat results agree within ±20% of their mean for ≥67% of ISR samples. FAIL triggers investigation. NOT_APPLICABLE when isr_flag is false.']
  lloq decimal(18,6) [note: 'The lowest concentration of analyte in a sample that can be quantitatively determined with acceptable precision and accuracy for this validated method and run. Used to flag results as BLQ (below limit of quantification).']
  matrix_type varchar [note: 'Type of biological matrix from which the sample was derived and analyzed. Determines applicable method validation parameters and reference ranges. Maps to PCSPEC in CDISC SDTM PC domain.']
  nominal_time_point decimal(10,4) [note: 'The protocol-specified time point (in hours post-dose) at which the sample was scheduled to be collected (e.g., 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 4.0, 8.0, 24.0). Used as the reference for PK modeling and deviation calculation. Maps to PCTPTNUM in CDISC SDTM PC domain.']
  numeric_result decimal(18,6) [note: 'Numeric result; implements SDTM PC.PCSTRESN']
  qc_sample_performance varchar [note: 'Overall acceptance outcome for the QC samples (low, medium, high QC) within the analytical run. PASS indicates ≥67% of QC samples within ±15% of nominal with at least 50% at each level passing. FAIL invalidates the run. MARGINAL triggers scientific review.']
  result_category varchar [note: 'High-level classification of the bioanalytical result type: PK_CONCENTRATION (pharmacokinetic drug/metabolite concentration), BIOMARKER (pharmacodynamic or disease biomarker), IMMUNOGENICITY (anti-drug antibody or neutralizing antibody), EXPLORATORY']
  result_comment varchar [note: 'Free-text comment entered by the bioanalytical scientist or laboratory reviewer providing additional context for the result (e.g., instrument flags, unusual chromatography, sample appearance notes). Maps to PCORRES or PCCOMMENT in CDISC SDTM PC domain.']
  result_reported_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the validated bioanalytical result was formally reported and released by the laboratory to the sponsor or data management team. Marks the transition from laboratory-internal to reportable status.']
  result_status varchar [note: 'Current disposition status of the bioanalytical result indicating whether it is reportable for inclusion in the clinical database, requires repeat analysis, or has been invalidated. Drives data flow into EDC and CDISC SDTM datasets.']
  result_unit varchar [note: 'Result unit; implements SDTM PC.PCSTRESU (CDISC CT UNIT codelist)']
  sample_stability_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the sample met stability criteria at the time of analysis based on validated short-term, long-term, and freeze-thaw stability data. False indicates a potential stability failure that may affect result validity.']
  sdtm_domain varchar [note: 'Target SDTM domain (PC); implements SDTM Dataset.DOMAIN']
  subject_number varchar [note: 'Human-readable subject identifier (e.g., site-subject number such as 001-001) used in the clinical trial. Distinct from the surrogate subject_id; used for cross-system reconciliation and regulatory reporting.']
  time_deviation_hours decimal(10,4) [note: 'Deviation of the actual sample collection time from the nominal protocol-specified time point, expressed in hours (actual minus nominal). Positive values indicate late collection; negative values indicate early collection.']
  uloq decimal(18,6) [note: 'The highest concentration of analyte in a sample that can be quantitatively determined with acceptable precision and accuracy for this validated method and run. Results above ULOQ require dilution and re-analysis.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent modification to this bioanalytical result record. Required for audit trail compliance and incremental data pipeline processing in the Databricks silver layer.']

  Note: 'Transactional record of a bioanalytical or biomarker assay result from a clinical trial PK/PD, DMPK, or exploratory biomarker sample. Captures assay run ID, sample ID, analyte/biomarker measured, concentration or categorical result value, unit/scale'
}

Table laboratory.lab_kit {
  lab_kit_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique surrogate identifier for the laboratory collection kit master record. Primary key for the lab_kit entity.']
  clinical_trial_authorization_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to regulatory.clinical_trial_authorization. Business justification: EU CTAs and substantial modifications must list investigational medicinal product (IMP) and ancillary material kits.']
  document_sop_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to document.document_sop. Business justification: Lab kits must be assembled, labeled, and distributed per specific SOPs governing kit preparation and handling. GCP requires kit handling procedures to be documented and traceable.']
  epoch_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to study.epoch. Business justification: Lab kits are epoch-specific (screening kits, treatment kits, follow-up kits have different components and expiry requirements).']
  lab_facility_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to laboratory.lab_facility. Business justification: A laboratory collection kit is supplied by and associated with a specific central laboratory facility. The central_lab_code STRING column is a denormalized reference to lab_facility.']
  lab_panel_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the laboratory panel definition that this kit is designed to support. Ensures correct collection materials are used per protocol-specified assays.']
  protocol_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to study.protocol. Business justification: Lab kits are designed and versioned per protocol specification (tube types, volumes, handling instructions).']
  regulatory_protocol_amendment_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to regulatory.regulatory_protocol_amendment. Business justification: Regulatory protocol amendments that change specimen collection procedures (tube type, volume, timing) require new lab kit versions.']
  study_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the clinical study for which this kit is designated. Links the kit to a specific protocol and sponsor.']
  study_site_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the clinical site to which this kit is assigned or shipped. Supports site-level inventory tracking.']
  treatment_arm_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to randomization.treatment_arm. Business justification: Lab kits are designed and assigned per treatment arm — active arm kits may require different tube types, volumes, or preservatives than placebo arm kits.']
  approved_date date [note: 'Date on which the kit design and components list was formally approved by the sponsor or quality team for use in the study. Supports audit trail and regulatory inspection readiness.']
  biohazard_classification varchar [note: 'IATA/UN biohazard classification for shipping the collected specimen (Category A UN2814, Category B UN3373, Exempt). Determines packaging and shipping documentation requirements for specimen transport.']
  cdisc_lbspec_code varchar [note: 'CDISC specimen type code; implements SDTM LB.LBSPEC (CDISC CT SPECTYPE codelist)']
  collection_timepoint varchar [note: 'Specific timepoint within a visit at which the specimen should be collected (e.g., pre-dose, 1h post-dose, 4h post-dose). Particularly relevant for PK/PD sampling schedules.']
  components_description varchar [note: 'Free-text or structured description of all components included in the kit (e.g., EDTA tubes, serum separator tubes, cryovials, dry ice packs, biohazard bags, requisition forms, instruction leaflets). Supports site training and deviation investigation.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when the lab kit master record was first created in the system. Part of the mandatory audit trail for GCP compliance and 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records requirements.']
  expiry_date date [note: 'Date after which the kit must not be used for specimen collection. Expiry is driven by the stability of collection tubes, preservatives, and reagents. Sites must discard or return kits past this date.']
  fasting_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the subject must be fasting prior to specimen collection using this kit. Fasting status affects reference ranges and result interpretation for metabolic and lipid panels.']
  is_ancillary_kit boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this kit is an ancillary/backup kit (True) rather than a primary protocol-required kit (False). Ancillary kits are used for repeat collections or unscheduled assessments.']
  kit_category varchar [note: 'Functional category of the kit indicating the scientific purpose of the specimen collection (e.g., Pharmacokinetics (PK), Pharmacodynamics (PD), safety labs, biomarker, genetic). Aligns kit to the study\'s analytical objectives.']
  kit_label_language varchar [note: 'ISO 639 language code for the primary language of the kit label and instruction leaflet (e.g., en, fr, de, ja). Ensures regulatory compliance for multi-country trials requiring local language labelling.']
  kit_number varchar [note: 'Externally-known unique alphanumeric identifier assigned to the kit, typically printed on the kit label and used for chain-of-custody tracking. Corresponds to the kit barcode or label ID in RTSM/IRT systems such as Medidata Rave RTSM.']
  kit_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the kit. Drives inventory management workflows and ensures expired or quarantined kits are not used for specimen collection. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: available|assigned|shipped|received|used|expired|quarantined|destroyed|returned —']
  kit_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the kit by specimen matrix type (e.g., blood, urine, tissue). Determines the collection containers and preservatives included. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: blood|urine|saliva|tissue|csf|stool|buccal_swab|plasma|serum|other — promote to reference']
  kit_version varchar [note: 'Version identifier of the kit design or configuration. Used to track protocol amendments that change collection requirements, ensuring sites use the correct kit version per the current protocol.']
  lab_accreditation_standard varchar [note: 'Accreditation standard under which the central laboratory processing specimens from this kit is certified (e.g., ISO 15189, CAP, CLIA, GCLP). Required for regulatory submissions and sponsor quality oversight.']
  lot_number varchar [note: 'Manufacturing lot number assigned by the kit supplier or central laboratory. Enables traceability for quality investigations, recalls, and regulatory inspections. Critical for ALCOA+ compliance.']
  manufacture_date date [note: 'Date on which the kit was manufactured or assembled by the supplier. Used in conjunction with expiry date to calculate shelf life and manage inventory rotation.']
  preservative_type varchar [note: 'Type of preservative or additive included in the kit (e.g., EDTA, heparin, sodium fluoride, formalin, RNAlater). Critical for specimen stability and downstream analytical method compatibility.']
  protocol_visit_reference varchar [note: 'Protocol-defined visit name or visit window for which this kit is intended (e.g., Screening, Day 1, Week 4). Ensures the correct kit type is used at the correct study visit per the protocol schedule of assessments.']
  quantity_per_shipment varchar [note: 'Standard number of kits included in a single shipment to a site. Used for supply planning, purchase order generation, and site inventory management.']
  reorder_threshold varchar [note: 'Minimum quantity of kits at a site below which a resupply order should be triggered. Supports proactive inventory management to prevent site stock-outs.']
  requisition_form_included boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a laboratory requisition form (paper or pre-printed label) is included in the kit. Requisition forms are required by central labs for specimen processing and chain-of-custody documentation.']
  return_kit_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the used kit or residual materials must be returned to the central laboratory or sponsor after specimen collection. Relevant for chain-of-custody and waste management compliance.']
  storage_condition varchar [note: 'Categorical storage condition required for the kit (e.g., refrigerated 2–8°C, frozen −20°C, room temperature). Complements the numeric temperature range with a human-readable label for site staff.']
  storage_temperature_max_c decimal(5,2) [note: 'Maximum allowable storage temperature in degrees Celsius for the kit. Used alongside minimum temperature to define the acceptable storage range and trigger excursion alerts.']
  storage_temperature_min_c decimal(5,2) [note: 'Minimum allowable storage temperature in degrees Celsius for the kit. Ensures cold-chain integrity and preservative efficacy. Deviations must be documented per GCP.']
  supplier_kit_catalog_number varchar [note: 'Supplier\'s own catalog or part number for this kit configuration. Used for reordering, purchase orders in the source system supplier quality documentation.']
  supplier_name varchar [note: 'Name of the vendor or central laboratory that manufactured and supplied the kit. Used for procurement, quality investigations, and supplier qualification tracking.']
  tube_count varchar [note: 'Total number of collection tubes included in the kit. Used for inventory reconciliation and to verify completeness of kit contents upon receipt at the site.']
  tube_type varchar [note: 'Type of collection tube(s) included in the kit (e.g., EDTA K2, SST, lithium heparin, sodium citrate, PAXgene). Determines anticoagulant or additive present, which is critical for assay validity.']
  tube_volume_ml decimal(6,2) [note: 'Nominal volume in millilitres of each collection tube in the kit. Used to confirm adequate sample volume for the required assays and to flag insufficient sample at processing.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when the lab kit master record was last modified. Supports change tracking, audit trail requirements, and incremental data loading in the Databricks Silver layer.']

  Note: 'Master record for laboratory collection kits supplied to clinical sites for specimen collection. Captures kit type, kit lot number, components list (tubes, containers, preservatives, requisition forms), storage requirements, expiry date, kit version, and'
}

  data_correction_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the resolution of this query resulted in a data value change in the source EDC or LIMS record. True = a data correction was made; False = original data confirmed or query cancelled without change. Key metric for data quality reporting.']

  ecrf_field_name varchar [note: 'Specific field name within the eCRF form that contains the queried laboratory data value (e.g., \'LBORRES\', \'LBORRESU\'). Enables precise identification of the data point in question for site response and EDC correction.']

  Note: 'Transactional record of a data query raised against a laboratory result in the EDC (Medidata Rave) or LIMS. Captures query ID, query type (missing value/implausible result/unit mismatch/collection time deviation), query text, raised by (data'
