  randomization_algorithm varchar [note: 'The randomization algorithm applied in conjunction with this stratification factor: \'permuted_block\' for block randomization within strata, \'minimization\' for adaptive minimization, \'stratified_block\' for stratified permuted block, \'dynamic_allocation\'']
  rtsm_factor_code varchar [note: 'The native identifier assigned to this stratification factor within the source RTSM/IRT system (e.g., Medidata Rave RTSM internal factor ID or the source system factor GUID). Used for system integration, reconciliation, and audit trail linkage.']
  rtsm_system varchar [note: 'Identifies the RTSM/IRT/IVRS system in which this stratification factor is configured and operationalized for subject randomization and kit assignment.']
  sap_section_reference varchar [note: 'Reference to the specific section of the Statistical Analysis Plan that describes the use of this stratification factor in primary and sensitivity analyses (e.g., \'the source system Stratification\'). Supports regulatory audit traceability.']
  sdtm_variable varchar [note: 'Target SDTM variable name for this stratification factor; implements SDTM variable reference.']
  sort_order varchar [note: 'Integer defining the display and processing sequence of this stratification factor within the randomization scheme. Lower values appear first in RTSM screens, the source system stratification matrix axes.']
  unit_of_imbalance varchar [note: 'Specifies whether the max_imbalance_threshold is expressed as a \'percentage\' of subjects within the stratum or as an absolute \'subject_count\'. Determines how the RTSM system evaluates balance during randomization.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this stratification factor record was last modified in the data platform. Tracks configuration changes and supports change control audit trail under 21 CFR Part 11.']
  validation_rule varchar [note: 'Business rule or logical expression applied to validate the stratification factor value at the time of randomization (e.g., \'BMIBL >= 18 AND BMIBL < 30\'). Prevents invalid factor assignments and ensures data integrity per ALCOA+ principles.']
  version_number varchar [note: 'Version identifier of this stratification factor definition, incremented with each protocol amendment or RTSM configuration change (e.g., \'1.0\', \'2.0\'). Supports change control and audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11.']

  Note: 'Defines the stratification factors used in a randomization scheme, including factor name, factor code, data source (eCRF field reference), factor type (categorical, continuous-binned), enumerated levels (level code, label, sort order, active status), and'
}

  sequence_within_block varchar [note: 'The position of this subject\'s allocation within the randomization block. Confidential to preserve blinding integrity. Used post-DBL for randomization quality review and biostatistical verification.']
  source_record_reference varchar [note: 'The native primary key or record identifier of this randomization event in the originating source system (Medidata Rave RTSM or the source system Enables bidirectional traceability between the lakehouse Silver layer and the operational system.']
  stratification_factor_1_value decimal(18,2) [note: 'The value of the first protocol-defined stratification factor captured at the time of randomization (e.g., disease severity: mild/moderate/severe). Stored individually to support stratification balance analytics and CDISC SDTM SUPPRAND dataset generation.']
  stratification_factor_2_value decimal(18,2) [note: 'The value of the second protocol-defined stratification factor captured at the time of randomization (e.g., geographic region: North America/Europe/Asia-Pacific). Supports stratification balance reporting and CDISC SDTM SUPPRAND.']
  stratification_factor_3_value decimal(18,2) [note: 'The value of the third protocol-defined stratification factor captured at the time of randomization (e.g., prior treatment: yes/no). Nullable when fewer than three stratification factors are defined in the protocol.']
  subject_number varchar [note: 'Subject identifier; implements SDTM DM.SUBJID; person-identifying (PII).']
  unblinding_reason varchar [note: 'The documented reason for breaking the blind for this subject\'s randomization. Null if still blinded. Required for regulatory audit trail and DSMB/DMC reporting.']
  unblinding_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time at which the blinding was broken for this subject\'s randomization. Null if the subject remains blinded. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time at which this randomization record was last modified in the Silver layer lakehouse. Tracks data corrections, status transitions, and unblinding events. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.']

  Note: 'Transactional record of a subject\'s randomization or re-randomization event. Captures the subject identifier, study site, randomization number assigned, treatment arm allocated, stratification cell, randomization timestamp, IRT/IVRS transaction reference'
}

Business justification: IRT dispensing and randomization transactions occur under a country-specific CTA. Regulatory compliance requires confirming the CTA was active at transaction time.']

  irt_system_reference_number varchar [note: 'The externally-known unique transaction reference number assigned by the IRT/IVRS/RTSM system (e.g., Medidata Rave RTSM transaction ID). Used for cross-system reconciliation and audit trail.']
  irt_system_version varchar [note: 'The validated version of the IRT/RTSM system at the time the transaction was executed. Required for regulatory submission traceability and system validation documentation per 21 CFR Part 11.']
  kit_number varchar [note: 'The unique identifier of the investigational product kit assigned to the subject during this IRT transaction. Links to the supply chain domain for kit tracking, expiry management, and depot reconciliation.']
  kit_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the investigational product kit assigned (e.g., active, placebo, rescue medication, titration pack). Supports supply chain analytics and blinding verification.']
  notes varchar [note: 'Free-text field for additional comments or annotations entered by the operator at the time of the IRT transaction. Captures contextual information not covered by structured fields, such as site-specific circumstances.']
  operator_role varchar [note: 'The functional role of the operator who performed the IRT transaction (e.g., Clinical Research Coordinator (CRC), Clinical Research Associate (CRA), Principal Investigator (PI), pharmacist). Supports access control auditing and GCP compliance.']

  subject_number varchar [note: 'Subject identifier; implements SDTM DM.SUBJID; person-identifying (PII).']
  transaction_outcome varchar [note: 'The technical outcome of the IRT transaction as reported by the RTSM system, indicating whether the transaction was successfully processed or encountered an error condition. Distinct from transaction_status which reflects the business lifecycle state.']
  transaction_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of the IRT transaction indicating whether it was successfully processed, failed, cancelled, or is pending confirmation in the RTSM system.']
  transaction_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The precise date and time (with timezone offset) at which the IRT/IVRS/RTSM transaction event occurred in the source system. This is the principal real-world business event time, distinct from record audit timestamps.']
  transaction_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the IRT transaction indicating the business event performed. Drives downstream processing logic for supply management and randomization audit.']
  unblinding_reason varchar [note: 'The documented reason for emergency unblinding of a subject\'s treatment assignment (e.g., SAE requiring knowledge of treatment, DSMB review). Populated only when blinding_status is unblinded.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this IRT transaction record was last modified in the data platform. Tracks corrections, reversals, or status updates applied after initial capture.']

  Note: 'Detailed log of all IRT/IVRS/RTSM system transactions related to randomization and kit dispensing. Captures transaction type (randomization, re-randomization, cancellation, kit assignment, dose change, titration), transaction timestamp, IRT system'
}

  unblinding_reason varchar [note: 'The documented reason for emergency or planned unblinding of the kit assignment, if applicable (e.g., \'SAE requiring treatment knowledge\', \'Study completion\', \'DSMB review\'). Null if the kit remains blinded.']

  Note: 'Records the assignment of an investigational medicinal product (IMP) kit to a subject at a specific visit, as triggered by the IRT/RTSM system following randomization or resupply.'

  Note: 'Defines the blinding configuration for a randomization scheme, including blinding type (open-label, single-blind, double-blind, triple-blind), blinded roles (subject, investigator, sponsor, CRA, statistician), blinding method (identical packaging, dummy'

  investigational_site_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to site.investigational_site. Business justification: Unblinding requests must originate from authorized study team members. Linking to study_assignment confirms the requestor\'s active, authorized role on the study — a GCP and']
  lab_result_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to laboratory.lab_result. Business justification: Emergency unblinding requests triggered by critical lab findings (e.g., severe hepatotoxicity, critical hematology values) must document the specific lab result that justified']
  principal_investigator_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to site.principal_investigator. Business justification: GCP requires PI accountability for emergency unblinding requests. Regulatory documentation mandates PI signature on unblinding forms.']
  protocol_deviation_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to compliance.protocol_deviation. Business justification: Unblinding events outside of emergency criteria or pre-specified procedures constitute protocol deviations.']
  quality_event_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to compliance.quality_event. Business justification: Unplanned or procedurally non-compliant unblinding events are captured as quality events in the QMS regardless of whether they constitute protocol deviations.']
  serious_adverse_event_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the Serious Adverse Event record that triggered an emergency unblinding request. Null when the unblinding reason is not SAE-driven (e.g., planned DBL unblinding or interim analysis).']
  sop_version_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to document.version. Business justification: GCP requires audit trails capturing which specific SOP version governed each unblinding request at the time of submission.']

  tmf_document_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to document.tmf_document. Business justification: Emergency and non-emergency unblinding requests with their outcomes are GCP-required records that must be filed in the eTMF as essential documents.']
  trial_subject_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the trial subject (patient) whose treatment assignment is being unblinded. Applicable for single-subject emergency unblinding events; may be null for planned study-level unblinding (e.g., DBL or interim analysis).']
  approval_level_count varchar [note: 'Total number of approval levels required for this unblinding request based on the study protocol and urgency classification. Drives the multi-step approval workflow routing in the RTSM system.']
  approver_1_decision varchar [note: 'Decision rendered by the first-level approver on the unblinding request. Approved advances the request; rejected terminates it; escalated routes to a higher authority; deferred postpones pending additional information.']
  approver_1_rationale varchar [note: 'Free-text rationale provided by the first-level approver explaining their decision. Required for GCP compliance and regulatory audit trail, particularly for rejections and escalations.']
  approver_1_role varchar [note: 'Clinical or organizational role of the first-level approver at the time of their decision. Captured at decision time for audit trail integrity. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: medical_monitor|sponsor_representative|cro_medical_director|irb_chair|dsmb_member|other —']
  approver_1_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the first-level approver rendered their decision. Used to calculate approval cycle time and assess compliance with urgency SLAs.']
  approver_2_decision varchar [note: 'Decision rendered by the second-level approver on the unblinding request. Follows the same decision taxonomy as level 1. Null when a second approval level is not required.']
  approver_2_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the second-level approver rendered their decision. Null when a second approval level is not required.']
  blinding_broken_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the blinding was actually broken as a result of this request (True) or whether the request was resolved without revealing the treatment assignment (False). Used for protocol deviation tracking and blinding integrity reporting.']
  clinical_justification varchar [note: 'Free-text narrative provided by the requestor describing the clinical rationale for unblinding. For SAE-driven requests, includes the nature of the adverse event, patient condition, and why knowledge of treatment assignment is medically necessary.']
  conditions_of_approval varchar [note: 'Any conditions or restrictions imposed by the approver(s) on the approved unblinding (e.g., \'information to be shared only with treating physician\', \'subject must be discontinued from study\').']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when this unblinding request record was first created in the lakehouse silver layer. Supports data lineage, audit trail, and 21 CFR Part 11 electronic record requirements.']
  current_approval_level varchar [note: 'The approval step currently pending action within the multi-level approval chain. Increments as each approver completes their review. Used for workflow routing and escalation monitoring.']
  dsmb_dmc_referral_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this unblinding request was referred to or reviewed by the DSMB/DMC (True) or not (False). Applicable for interim analysis unblinding or escalated emergency cases requiring independent oversight.']
  final_outcome varchar [note: 'The definitive resolution of the unblinding request after all approval levels have been completed. Approved means the treatment assignment was revealed; rejected means the request was denied; withdrawn means the requestor retracted the request; escalated']
  irb_iec_notification_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the IRB/IEC must be notified of this unblinding event per the study protocol or applicable regulations (True) or not (False). Drives regulatory notification workflow.']
  irb_iec_notification_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the IRB/IEC was formally notified of the unblinding event. Null if notification is not required or has not yet been sent. Used for regulatory compliance tracking.']
  protocol_deviation_raised boolean [note: 'Indicates whether an unplanned or unauthorized unblinding event associated with this request resulted in a protocol deviation being raised (True) or not (False). Links to the compliance domain for deviation tracking.']
  request_number varchar [note: 'Human-readable, externally-known business identifier for the unblinding request, typically generated by the RTSM/IRT system (e.g., the source system or Medidata Rave). Used in regulatory correspondence, audit trails, and DSMB/DMC communications.']
  request_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of the unblinding request workflow. Tracks progression from initial submission through multi-level approval to final resolution. Drives GCP audit trail and DSMB/DMC oversight reporting.']
  requestor_name varchar [note: 'Full name of the individual who submitted the unblinding request, captured at the time of submission for audit trail integrity per 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ requirements. Preserved even if the workforce record is later modified.']
  requestor_role varchar [note: 'Clinical role of the individual who submitted the unblinding request at the time of submission. Captured at request time to preserve audit integrity even if the person\'s role changes later.']
  required_by_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time by which the unblinding decision is clinically required, as specified by the requestor. Used to enforce urgency SLAs and escalation triggers. For emergency requests, this may be within hours of submission.']
  source_system_request_code varchar [note: 'The native identifier of this unblinding request in the originating operational system (the source system or Medidata Rave RTSM). Used for cross-system reconciliation and data lineage tracing in the lakehouse.']
  sponsor_notification_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the study sponsor was formally notified of the unblinding event. Required for emergency unblinding events per GCP and sponsor agreements. Null if not yet notified.']
  submitted_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the unblinding request was formally submitted by the requestor in the RTSM/IRT system. This is the principal business event timestamp for this transaction.']
  treatment_arm_revealed varchar [note: 'The treatment arm or randomization code revealed upon approved unblinding (e.g., \'Active Drug A 10mg\', \'Placebo\', \'Comparator B\'). Populated only when final_outcome is \'approved\'. Highly sensitive as it compromises blinding integrity for the subject.']
  unblinding_reason varchar [note: 'Categorical classification of the clinical or regulatory justification for the unblinding request. Drives urgency classification and approval routing. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE']
  unblinding_scope varchar [note: 'Indicates whether the unblinding request pertains to a single subject (emergency or medical necessity) or to the entire study (planned events such as Database Lock, interim analysis, or final analysis).']
  unblinding_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the treatment assignment was actually revealed to the authorized recipient. Null if the request was rejected or withdrawn. Critical for GCP audit trail and regulatory reporting timelines.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when this unblinding request record was most recently modified in the lakehouse silver layer. Tracks the latest state change for audit trail and data quality monitoring.']
  urgency_level varchar [note: 'Clinical urgency classification of the unblinding request. Emergency indicates immediate patient safety risk requiring unblinding within hours; urgent indicates within 24 hours; routine indicates planned/scheduled unblinding with no immediate safety']
  withdrawal_reason varchar [note: 'Free-text explanation provided by the requestor when withdrawing an unblinding request before final resolution. Null when the request was not withdrawn. Required for audit trail completeness.']

  Note: 'Transactional record of a request to unblind a subject\'s treatment assignment, encompassing the full request-through-resolution lifecycle including multi-level approval steps.'
}

Table randomization.unblinding_approval {
  unblinding_approval_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique surrogate identifier for each unblinding approval record in the randomization domain. Primary key for this entity.']
  document_sop_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to document.document_sop. Business justification: Unblinding approvals must follow a documented SOP per GCP and sponsor SOPs. unblinding_approval has no document_sop_id despite having gcp_compliance_confirmed and']

  study_site_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the investigational site where the subject is enrolled and where the unblinding event is occurring.']
  subject_randomization_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the subject\'s randomization record whose treatment arm assignment is the subject of the unblinding request. Links to the randomization domain for treatment arm and kit assignment context.']

  unblinding_request_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the parent unblinding request that this approval decision is associated with. Links the approval record to the originating request in the multi-level approval workflow.']
  approval_conditions varchar [note: 'Free-text description of any conditions or restrictions attached to a conditional approval decision (e.g., \'Unblinding permitted only to treating physician; sponsor team remains blinded\'). Populated only when approval_status is conditionally_approved.']
  approval_level varchar [note: 'Numeric level within the multi-tier approval hierarchy (e.g., 1 = first-line approver such as PI, 2 = second-line such as Medical Monitor, 3 = final authority such as Sponsor Medical Officer).']
  approval_number varchar [note: 'Externally-known, human-readable unique identifier for this approval record, used in regulatory submissions, audit trails, and cross-system references (e.g., UBA-STUDY01-202401). Serves as the BUSINESS_IDENTIFIER for this transaction.']
  approval_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the unblinding approval decision. Reflects the outcome of the approver\'s review: approved (unblinding authorized), rejected (unblinding denied), escalated (referred to higher authority), pending (awaiting decision), withdrawn']
  approver_name varchar [note: 'Full name of the individual who rendered the approval or rejection decision. Required for GCP audit trail and 21 CFR Part 11 electronic signature attribution. Classified as confidential as it identifies a study personnel member.']
  approver_role varchar [note: 'The functional role of the individual who rendered the approval decision. Defines the authority level within the multi-level unblinding approval hierarchy.']
  blinding_maintained boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the overall study blinding integrity was maintained following this unblinding event (True = blinding maintained for the broader study population; False = blinding compromised at study level).']
  comments varchar [note: 'Additional free-text comments or observations recorded by the approver beyond the formal decision rationale. May include follow-up actions required, safety observations, or cross-references to related records.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this unblinding approval record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail completeness per ALCOA+ principles.']
  decision_rationale varchar [note: 'Free-text narrative explanation provided by the approver justifying the approval, rejection, escalation, or conditional approval decision. Required for GCP compliance and regulatory audit trail to demonstrate that the decision was medically and']
  decision_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The exact date and time (with timezone) at which the approver rendered their decision on the unblinding request. This is the principal business event timestamp for this transaction, critical for GCP audit trail and 21 CFR Part 11 electronic signature']
  delegation_of_authority boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the approver was acting under a formal delegation of authority (True = delegated authority; False = primary role holder). Relevant when a PI delegates unblinding approval authority to a sub-investigator or designee.']
  emergency_unblinding boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this unblinding approval was processed under emergency procedures (True = emergency unblinding bypassing standard multi-level approval; False = standard approval workflow).']
  escalation_reason varchar [note: 'Free-text explanation of why the approval decision was escalated to a higher authority rather than resolved at the current approval level. Populated only when approval_status is \'escalated\'.']
  escalation_target_role varchar [note: 'The role to which the unblinding decision has been escalated when approval_status is \'escalated\'. Identifies the next authority in the approval chain. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE']
  gcp_compliance_confirmed boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the approver explicitly confirmed that the unblinding procedure was conducted in accordance with Good Clinical Practice (GCP) guidelines and the applicable protocol SOP (True = confirmed; False = not confirmed or exception noted).']
  irb_iec_notification_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the Institutional Review Board (IRB) or Independent Ethics Committee (IEC) must be notified of this unblinding event per protocol or regulatory requirements (True = notification required; False = not required).']
  irb_iec_notified_date date [note: 'The date on which the Institutional Review Board (IRB) or Independent Ethics Committee (IEC) was formally notified of the unblinding event. Populated when irb_iec_notification_required is True and notification has been completed.']
  notification_sent boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the required regulatory and sponsor notifications were dispatched following this approval decision (True = notifications sent; False = pending notification). Supports compliance tracking for expedited safety reporting timelines.']
  notification_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time at which regulatory and sponsor notifications were dispatched following the approval decision. Populated when notification_sent is True. Used to verify compliance with expedited reporting timelines (e.g., 7-day/15-day SAE reporting).']
  protocol_version varchar [note: 'The version of the study protocol that was in effect at the time of the unblinding approval decision. Required to confirm that the unblinding procedure followed the correct protocol version\'s unblinding SOP.']
  response_time_hours decimal(10,2) [note: 'Elapsed time in hours between the submission of the unblinding request and the rendering of this approval decision. Used for KPI monitoring of emergency unblinding response times and SOP compliance.']
  signature_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The exact date and time at which the approver applied their 21 CFR Part 11-compliant electronic signature to the approval decision. May differ from decision_timestamp if signature was applied after the verbal/written decision.']
  source_system_record_code varchar [note: 'The native record identifier from the originating operational system (e.g., Medidata Rave workflow ID, the source system approval reference). Enables traceability from the Silver layer back to the system of record for audit and reconciliation.']
  treatment_arm_revealed varchar [note: 'The treatment arm or randomization code that was disclosed to the approver upon approval of the unblinding request (e.g., \'Active Drug A 10mg\', \'Placebo\'). Populated only after approval is granted and unblinding is executed.']
  unblinding_reason_category varchar [note: 'Categorical classification of the reason driving the unblinding request being reviewed. Supports regulatory reporting and trend analysis of unblinding events.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this unblinding approval record was last modified. Supports audit trail integrity and change detection per 21 CFR Part 11.']

  Note: 'Records the approval or rejection decision for an unblinding request. Captures the approver role (medical monitor, PI, sponsor medical officer), decision (approved, rejected, escalated), decision rationale, decision timestamp, and any conditions attached'
}

Table regulatory.submission {

  tmf_document_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to document.tmf_document. Business justification: Each regulatory submission generates essential TMF documents (cover letters, agency correspondence, submission confirmations) that must be filed per ICH E6 GCP.']

  notes varchar [note: 'Free-text field for capturing additional context, internal commentary, or regulatory strategy notes associated with this submission event. Not transmitted to the agency; for internal regulatory operations use only.']
  number varchar [note: 'Externally-known unique identifier for this submission as assigned by the health authority or internal tracking system (e.g., IND number, NDA number, sequence number within an eCTD dossier). Used for cross-referencing with agency correspondence.']

  approval_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the regulatory approval or authorization received. Distinguishes between IND allowance (Investigational New Drug), NDA approval (New Drug Application), BLA approval (Biologics License Application), MAA approval (Marketing Authorization']
  approved_dose varchar [note: 'The approved dose or dose range as specified in the regulatory approval (e.g., \'10 mg once daily\', \'200 mg/m² every 3 weeks\'). Captures the label-approved dosing regimen for the approved indication and population.']
  approved_indication varchar [note: 'The specific disease, condition, or therapeutic indication for which the health authority has granted approval. Reflects the exact label language or CTA scope as approved (e.g., \'Treatment of moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis in adults\').']
  approved_population varchar [note: 'Description of the patient population covered by the approval, including age group, disease severity, prior treatment requirements, or other eligibility criteria as specified in the approved label or CTA (e.g., \'Adults ≥18 years with inadequate response']
  compliance_inspection_code varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to compliance.inspection. Business justification: Pre-approval inspections (PAIs) are a standard FDA/EMA step before granting marketing approval.']
  conditions_of_approval varchar [note: 'Narrative description of any conditions, restrictions, or requirements attached to the approval by the health authority (e.g., REMS requirements, restricted distribution, mandatory risk minimization measures, specific labeling requirements).']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp when this regulatory approval record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ data integrity principles.']
  dosage_form varchar [note: 'The pharmaceutical dosage form approved by the health authority (e.g., tablet, capsule, injection, infusion, patch). Reflects the specific formulation covered by the approval as stated in the approved label.']
  drug_name varchar [note: 'The International Nonproprietary Name (INN) or brand name of the drug, biologic, or investigational medicinal product covered by this approval. Denormalized for regulatory reporting and label management.']
  effective_date date [note: 'The date from which the regulatory approval becomes legally effective and the sponsor may act upon it (e.g., commence the trial, market the product). May differ from the agency decision date for conditional or phased approvals.']
  expiry_date date [note: 'The date on which the regulatory approval expires or requires renewal (applicable to CTAs, annual IND renewals, and time-limited authorizations). Null for indefinite approvals such as standard NDA/BLA marketing authorizations.']
  geographic_scope varchar [note: 'Description of the geographic territory or jurisdictions covered by this approval (e.g., \'United States\', \'European Union - 27 Member States\', \'Japan\'). Supports multi-regional regulatory portfolio management.']
  inn_code varchar [note: 'The WHO-assigned International Nonproprietary Name (INN) code or identifier for the active substance covered by this approval. Supports WHO-DD coding and cross-study drug identification.']
  inspection_readiness_status varchar [note: 'Current inspection readiness status for this approval record, indicating whether all supporting documentation in the eTMF is complete and audit-ready for potential agency inspection. Supports GCP inspection preparedness.']
  irb_iec_reference varchar [note: 'Reference number or identifier of the corresponding IRB (Institutional Review Board) or IEC (Independent Ethics Committee) approval associated with this regulatory authorization. Supports ethics and regulatory approval alignment tracking.']
  is_conditional_approval boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this approval was granted conditionally (True) or as a full unconditional approval (False). Conditional approvals require the sponsor to fulfill specific post-marketing commitments or confirmatory studies.']
  is_renewal_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this approval requires periodic renewal or re-authorization (True) or is granted indefinitely (False). Relevant for CTAs, annual IND reports, and time-limited authorizations in certain jurisdictions.']
  letter_date date [note: 'The date printed on the official agency approval letter or decision notice. May differ from the agency decision date if the letter was issued after the formal decision was recorded.']
  letter_reference varchar [note: 'Official reference number or document identifier of the agency approval letter or decision notice (e.g., FDA approval letter reference, EMA decision reference). Used to locate the source document in the eTMF or regulatory binder in Veeva Vault.']
  mah_name varchar [note: 'Name of the Marketing Authorization Holder.']
  notes varchar [note: 'Free-text field for additional regulatory context, internal commentary, or supplementary information about this approval that does not fit into structured fields. Used by regulatory affairs teams for operational notes.']
  number varchar [note: 'Externally-assigned unique identifier issued by the health authority for this approval (e.g., NDA 123456, EMA/H/C/004321, IND 12345). This is the official agency-assigned reference number used in all regulatory correspondence.']
  post_marketing_commitments varchar [note: 'Description of post-marketing study commitments, confirmatory trials, or pharmacovigilance obligations required by the health authority as a condition of approval. Includes Phase IV studies, REMS, and risk management plans.']
  protocol_amendment_version varchar [note: 'The version of the study protocol or protocol amendment that was in effect at the time of this approval. Relevant for CTA authorizations and protocol amendment approvals to ensure the correct protocol version is linked.']
  renewal_due_date date [note: 'The date by which the sponsor must submit a renewal application or annual report to maintain the validity of this approval. Null if renewal is not required. Critical for regulatory compliance tracking.']
  review_pathway varchar [note: 'The regulatory review pathway or designation under which the application was reviewed and approved (e.g., Standard, Priority Review, Accelerated Approval, Breakthrough Therapy, Fast Track, Orphan Drug).']
  sponsor_name varchar [note: 'Name of the sponsor organization for this approval.']
  therapeutic_area varchar [note: 'The therapeutic area or disease category associated with the approved indication (e.g., Oncology, Cardiovascular, Immunology, Neurology, Infectious Disease). Used for portfolio analytics and regulatory strategy reporting.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp when this regulatory approval record was most recently modified. Supports audit trail requirements and change tracking under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ data integrity principles.']

  Note: 'Records regulatory approvals, authorizations, and decisions received from health authorities. Captures approval type (IND allowance, NDA approval, MAA approval, CTA authorization, label approval), approval date, effective date, approved indication'
}

Table regulatory.ind_application {
  ind_application_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique surrogate identifier for the IND application record in the lakehouse silver layer. Primary key for this entity.']
  audit_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to compliance.audit. Business justification: IND applications require audit verification of manufacturing, preclinical, and early clinical data before FDA submission.']
  health_authority_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to regulatory.health_authority. Business justification: ind_application is filed with the FDA or equivalent competent authority but only stores regulatory_agency STRING. Normalize to a health_authority FK. No reverse FK exists.']
  nda_bla_application_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to regulatory.nda_bla_application. Business justification: An IND application is the precursor to an NDA/BLA application — the IND enables clinical trials that generate the data for the NDA/BLA.']
  parent_application_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the parent regulatory application record when this IND is a sub-application or cross-references a master NDA/BLA/MAA application. Enables hierarchical navigation of the regulatory application portfolio.']
  study_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key to the study this record belongs to, for study context and traceability.']
  tmf_document_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to document.tmf_document. Business justification: IND applications and their annual reports, safety updates, and FDA correspondence are essential TMF documents (TMF Zone 1).']
  amendment_count varchar [note: 'The cumulative number of IND amendments (protocol amendments, information amendments, safety reports) submitted to the FDA under this IND. Tracks the volume of regulatory activity and dossier complexity.']
  annual_report_due_date date [note: 'The next due date for the IND Annual Report submission to the FDA. Annual reports are required within 60 days of the anniversary of the IND effective date and must summarize clinical progress, safety data, and manufacturing updates.']
  application_country_code varchar [note: 'ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the jurisdiction in which this application is filed (e.g., USA for FDA, GBR for MHRA, JPN for PMDA). Enables multi-country regulatory portfolio analytics.']
  breakthrough_therapy_designation boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the FDA has granted Breakthrough Therapy designation for the investigational product under this IND. Breakthrough Therapy designation provides intensive FDA guidance and rolling review for drugs showing substantial improvement over']
  clinical_hold_date date [note: 'The date on which the FDA issued a clinical hold order on this IND, halting enrollment or dosing of subjects. Nullable for INDs not on clinical hold. Triggers mandatory sponsor response within 30 days.']
  clinical_hold_lifted_date date [note: 'The date on which the FDA lifted the clinical hold and authorized resumption of clinical trials under this IND. Nullable for INDs that have never been on clinical hold or where the hold remains active.']
  clinical_hold_reason varchar [note: 'Description of the FDA\'s stated reason for imposing a clinical hold on this IND. Captures the safety concern, protocol deficiency, or regulatory non-compliance issue cited by the agency. Nullable for INDs not on clinical hold.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp when this IND application record was first created in the lakehouse data platform. Represents the RECORD_AUDIT_CREATED category for audit trail and data lineage purposes. Conforms to 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records requirements.']
  dosage_form varchar [note: 'The pharmaceutical dosage form of the investigational product (e.g., tablet, capsule, injection, infusion, patch). Captured from the IND CMC section and used for supply chain and regulatory tracking.']
  drug_substance_name varchar [note: 'International Nonproprietary Name (INN) or chemical name of the active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) covered under this IND. Used for regulatory cross-referencing and WHO-DD coding.']
  ectd_submission_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this IND application is submitted in eCTD format via the FDA Electronic Submissions Gateway. True indicates eCTD format; False indicates paper or non-eCTD electronic submission. FDA mandates eCTD for most IND submissions.']
  effective_date date [note: 'The date on which the IND became effective and clinical trials were authorized to commence. Under 21 CFR Part 312.40, an IND becomes effective 30 days after FDA receipt unless FDA places a clinical hold.']
  equivalent_application_number varchar [note: 'The application number assigned by a non-FDA regulatory agency for an equivalent authorization (e.g., EMA CTA number, MHRA CTA reference, PMDA CTN). Used to cross-reference the IND with parallel international submissions.']
  fast_track_designation boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the FDA has granted Fast Track designation for the investigational product under this IND. Fast Track facilitates development and expedites review of drugs treating serious conditions with unmet medical need.']
  fda_application_receipt_date date [note: 'The date on which the FDA officially acknowledged receipt of the IND application. Starts the 30-day review clock per 21 CFR Part 312.40. May differ from the initial submission date if there were transmission delays.']
  fda_division varchar [note: 'The FDA Center and Division responsible for reviewing this IND application (e.g., CDER/Division of Oncology Products 1, CBER/Division of Vaccines). Determines the regulatory review team and applicable FDA guidance documents.']
  inactivation_date date [note: 'The date on which the IND was placed into inactive status, either by sponsor notification or FDA action. Nullable for active INDs. Represents the EFFECTIVE_UNTIL boundary for the active IND period.']
  ind_number varchar [note: 'Official IND number assigned by the FDA upon receipt of the IND application. This is the externally-known regulatory identifier used in all agency correspondence, safety reports, and annual reports.']
  ind_serial_number_latest varchar [note: 'The most recent serial number assigned to the latest IND submission sequence (original or amendment). IND submissions are numbered sequentially starting from 0000. Used to track the current version of the IND dossier in Veeva Vault eTMF.']
  ind_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the IND application by its intended purpose. Commercial INDs are filed by pharmaceutical/biotech sponsors for drug development. Research INDs are filed by investigators for academic studies.']
  indication varchar [note: 'The specific disease, condition, or patient population for which the investigational product is being studied under this IND. Aligns with the MedDRA Preferred Term (PT) for the target indication.']
  initial_submission_date date [note: 'The date on which the original IND application was first submitted to the FDA. This is the principal business event date for the IND lifecycle and triggers the 30-day FDA review clock per 21 CFR Part 312.40.']
  investigational_product_code varchar [note: 'Internal sponsor code or development compound number assigned to the investigational product (e.g., ABC-123). Used for cross-referencing across clinical, regulatory, and supply chain systems including RTSM and the source system']
  investigational_product_name varchar [note: 'The name of the investigational drug, biologic, or compound covered under this IND application. May be a code name, generic name, or proprietary name as designated by the sponsor.']
  last_annual_report_date date [note: 'The date on which the most recent IND Annual Report was submitted to the FDA. Used to track compliance with annual reporting obligations and calculate the next due date.']
  orphan_drug_designation boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the FDA Office of Orphan Products Development (OOPD) has granted Orphan Drug designation for the investigational product. Orphan designation provides tax credits, market exclusivity, and expedited review for drugs targeting rare diseases']
  phase_coverage varchar [note: 'The clinical development phase(s) authorized under this IND application. An IND may cover a single phase or span multiple phases. Phase 1 covers first-in-human safety studies; Phase 2 covers efficacy and dose-ranging; Phase 3 covers confirmatory trials']
  protocol_count varchar [note: 'The total number of clinical study protocols currently authorized and active under this IND application. An IND may cover multiple protocols across different phases and indications.']
  safety_reporting_obligation varchar [note: 'Defines the IND-level safety reporting obligation tier. Standard obligations apply to all INDs. Expedited 7-day reporting applies to fatal or life-threatening unexpected SUSARs.']
  sponsor_contact_email varchar [note: 'Email address of the designated sponsor contact person for FDA correspondence related to this IND application. Used for regulatory notifications and agency communication tracking.']
  sponsor_contact_name varchar [note: 'Name of the sponsor contact person for this IND application.']
  sponsor_name varchar [note: 'Name of the sponsor organization for this IND application.']
  sponsor_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the sponsor organization type. Distinguishes between commercial pharmaceutical/biotech companies, academic institutions, government agencies, and Contract Research Organizations (CROs) acting as sponsor.']
  therapeutic_area varchar [note: 'The disease area or medical specialty that the investigational product targets (e.g., Oncology, Cardiology, Neurology, Infectious Disease). Used for portfolio analytics, regulatory strategy, and resource planning.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp when this IND application record was most recently modified in the lakehouse data platform. Represents the RECORD_AUDIT_UPDATED category. Used for incremental data pipeline processing and audit trail compliance per 21 CFR Part 11.']
  withdrawal_date date [note: 'The date on which the sponsor formally withdrew the IND application from FDA. Nullable for non-withdrawn INDs. Triggers archival obligations and cessation of all clinical activities under the IND.']

  Note: 'Specialized master record for Investigational New Drug (IND) applications filed with the FDA (or equivalent CTAs with EMA/MHRA). Tracks IND number, IND type (commercial, research, emergency), sponsor name, investigational product name, phase coverage'
}

  eudract_number varchar [note: 'European Union Drug Regulating Authorities Clinical Trials (EudraCT) number assigned to the clinical trial, used for EMA and EU member state safety report submissions. Format: YYYY-NNNNNN-CC.']
  expedited_report_timeline_days varchar [note: 'Regulatory reporting timeline in calendar days applicable to this expedited submission (typically 7 days for fatal/life-threatening unexpected SARs or 15 days for other unexpected serious adverse reactions). Null for periodic reports.']
  investigational_product_name varchar [note: 'Name of the investigational medicinal product (IMP) or drug substance that is the subject of this safety report. Aligns with the IND/CTA product designation.']
  is_expedited boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this safety report is an expedited submission (True) subject to 7-day or 15-day reporting timelines, as opposed to a periodic report. Expedited reports include SUSARs and IND safety reports for unexpected serious adverse reactions.']
  is_follow_up boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this submission is a follow-up (True) to a previously submitted safety report for the same event or reporting period, as opposed to an initial/original submission (False). Follow-up submissions provide updated or additional information.']
  listedness_assessment varchar [note: 'Assessment of whether the adverse reaction is listed (expected) or unlisted (unexpected) in the current Investigator\'s Brochure (IB) or Reference Safety Information (RSI).']
  meddra_pt_code varchar [note: 'Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) Preferred Term (PT) code for the primary adverse reaction or event described in this safety report. Standardizes event terminology for regulatory submissions and signal detection.']
  meddra_soc_code varchar [note: 'Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) System Organ Class (SOC) code associated with the primary adverse reaction in this safety report. Used for aggregate safety analysis and tabulation in periodic reports.']
  regulatory_action_description varchar [note: 'Free-text description of the regulatory action required or taken as a result of this safety report submission (e.g., IB update, protocol amendment, clinical hold notification, Dear Investigator Letter). Populated when regulatory_action_required is True.']
  regulatory_action_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this safety report submission has triggered or requires a regulatory action such as a protocol amendment, IB update, informed consent revision, or clinical hold. Supports inspection readiness and CAPA tracking.']
  report_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the safety report being submitted. IND_SAFETY_REPORT = expedited IND safety report (15-day/7-day); DSUR = Development Safety Update Report; PSUR_PBRER = Periodic Safety Update Report / Periodic Benefit-Risk Evaluation Report; SUSAR =']
  report_version varchar [note: 'Version identifier of the safety report document (e.g., 1.0, 2.0, 1.1 for amendments). Tracks original submissions versus follow-up or amended versions submitted to the same agency.']
  reporting_period_end_date date [note: 'End date of the data collection period covered by this safety report, also known as the data lock point (DLP). Defines the cut-off date for safety data included in the report.']
  reporting_period_start_date date [note: 'Start date of the data collection period covered by this safety report (e.g., the beginning of the DSUR or PSUR/PBRER data lock window). Applicable to periodic reports; may be null for expedited reports.']
  seriousness_criteria varchar [note: 'ICH E2A seriousness criterion that triggered the expedited reporting obligation for this submission. Applicable to SUSAR and IND safety reports. FATAL = resulted in death; LIFE_THREATENING = immediately life-threatening; HOSPITALIZATION = required or']
  submission_country_code varchar [note: 'ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the jurisdiction to which the safety report is submitted (e.g., USA, GBR, JPN, CAN, AUS). Supports multi-country submission tracking.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent update to this safety report submission record. Supports audit trail integrity and change tracking per 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ requirements.']
  veeva_vault_document_reference varchar [note: 'Document identifier in Veeva Vault (eTMF/regulatory submissions module) for the finalized safety report document. Enables direct traceability from this submission record to the source document in the system of record.']

  Note: 'Tracks regulatory safety report submissions including IND Annual Reports, Development Safety Update Reports (DSURs), Periodic Safety Update Reports (PSURs/PBRERs), and expedited SUSAR/IND safety reports.'
}

Table regulatory.clinical_trial_authorization {
  clinical_trial_authorization_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique surrogate identifier for the Clinical Trial Authorization record in the lakehouse Silver layer. Primary key for this entity.']

  submission_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to regulatory.submission. Business justification: A Clinical Trial Authorization is submitted to a national competent authority as a regulatory submission.']

  effective_from_date date [note: 'Date from which the Clinical Trial Authorization is legally effective and trial activities may commence in the member state. May differ from authorization_date if conditions or a deferred start apply.']

  expiry_date date [note: 'Date on which the Clinical Trial Authorization expires, after which trial activities in the member state are no longer authorized unless a renewal has been granted. Null for open-ended authorizations.']
  gdpr_data_transfer_mechanism varchar [note: 'Legal mechanism under GDPR used to authorize the transfer of personal data of EU trial subjects to non-EU countries in connection with this CTA. Required for EU-based trials involving cross-border data flows.']
  indication_meddra_code varchar [note: 'Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) Preferred Term (PT) code for the primary disease indication under investigation in this authorized trial. Enables standardized cross-study and cross-authority indication reporting.']
  inspection_readiness_status varchar [note: 'Current inspection readiness status for this CTA record, indicating whether the regulatory documentation and evidence supporting this authorization is ready for NCA or GCP inspection. Supports proactive inspection readiness management.']
  irb_iec_approval_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a separate Institutional Review Board (IRB) or Independent Ethics Committee (IEC) approval is required in addition to the NCA authorization in the member state. Relevant for countries with parallel ethics and regulatory review tracks.']
  member_state_code varchar [note: 'ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 or alpha-3 country code of the EU member state or non-EU country in which this Clinical Trial Authorization was granted by the national competent authority. Enables multi-country authorization tracking.']
  modification_scope varchar [note: 'Brief description of the scope of the substantial modification covered by this CTA record (e.g., protocol amendment, IMP change, new investigational site addition, safety update). Populated for substantial_modification authorization types.']
  national_portal_reference varchar [note: 'Reference number or identifier assigned by the national regulatory portal (e.g., MHRA IRAS number, BfArM reference, ANSM reference, Health Canada CTD number) for this CTA. Complements the CTIS trial ID for country-specific tracking.']
  planned_subject_count varchar [note: 'Number of trial subjects planned to be enrolled in the member state under this Clinical Trial Authorization, as declared in the approved protocol. Used for site capacity planning and regulatory reporting.']
  regulatory_framework varchar [note: 'Primary regulatory framework under which this Clinical Trial Authorization was granted (e.g., EU CTR 536/2014, national regulation, ISO 14155 for medical devices). Determines applicable procedural and reporting requirements.']
  sponsor_protocol_number varchar [note: 'Internal protocol identifier assigned by the sponsor or CRO to uniquely identify the study protocol associated with this CTA. Used to link the authorization to the study protocol design and development records.']
  submission_date date [note: 'Date on which the Clinical Trial Authorization application was formally submitted to the national competent authority. Used to calculate regulatory review timelines and track compliance with submission deadlines.']
  substantial_modification_number varchar [note: 'Sequential identifier for substantial modifications to the original CTA, as assigned by the sponsor or NCA. Populated only for authorization_type = substantial_modification. Enables tracking of the amendment history chain.']
  suspension_date date [note: 'Date on which the Clinical Trial Authorization was suspended by the national competent authority or voluntarily by the sponsor. Null if the CTA has never been suspended. Triggers safety and compliance escalation workflows.']
  suspension_reason varchar [note: 'Narrative reason for the suspension of the Clinical Trial Authorization, as communicated by the national competent authority or sponsor. Populated only when suspension_date is not null.']
  therapeutic_area varchar [note: 'Therapeutic area or disease indication covered by the clinical trial authorized under this CTA (e.g., Oncology, Cardiology, Neurology, Infectious Disease). Used for portfolio analytics and regulatory reporting segmentation.']
  trial_phase varchar [note: 'Regulatory phase of the clinical trial covered by this authorization (Phase I through Phase IV), as defined by ICH E8 and applicable NCA guidelines. Determines applicable regulatory requirements, safety reporting thresholds, and monitoring intensity.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this Clinical Trial Authorization record was last modified in the lakehouse Silver layer. Supports audit trail, change tracking, and ALCOA+ compliance requirements.']
  validation_date date [note: 'Date on which the national competent authority confirmed the CTA application was formally valid and complete for review. Marks the start of the regulatory assessment clock under EU CTR 536/2014.']
  withdrawal_date date [note: 'Date on which the Clinical Trial Authorization was formally withdrawn, either by the sponsor or by the national competent authority. Null if the CTA has not been withdrawn.']
  withdrawal_reason varchar [note: 'Narrative reason for the withdrawal of the Clinical Trial Authorization. Populated only when withdrawal_date is not null. Required for regulatory reporting and inspection readiness.']

  Note: 'Master record for Clinical Trial Authorizations (CTAs) issued by national competent authorities under EU CTR 536/2014, national regulations, and equivalent non-US frameworks.'
}

Table document.version {
  version_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique surrogate identifier for each discrete version record of a controlled document in the Trial Master File (TMF) or Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) library. Primary key of this table.']
  controlled_terminology_codelist_id varchar [note: 'Optional CDISC CT codelist governing categorical values on this record.']
  document_sop_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to document.document_sop. Business justification: The version table description explicitly states it tracks \'the full version history of every controlled document in the TMF and SOP library.\' Currently version only has tmf_document_id']
  tmf_document_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the parent document record for which this version was created. All versions of the same document share this identifier, enabling full version lineage reconstruction.']
  approved_date date [note: 'The date on which this document version received final approval and was authorized for use. Null if the version has not yet been approved. Supports 21 CFR Part 11 and EU CTR audit trail requirements.']
  approver_name varchar [note: 'Full name of the individual who granted final approval for this document version. Required for 21 CFR Part 11 electronic signature audit trail and GCP inspection readiness.']
  archival_status varchar [note: 'The archival lifecycle state of this document version. \'active\' = in current use; \'archived\' = moved to long-term archival storage per ICH GCP retention requirements; \'pending_archival\' = scheduled for archival; \'destroyed\' = permanently deleted per']
  author_name varchar [note: 'Full name of the individual who authored this document version. Captured as part of the ALCOA+ attributable audit trail. Typically a CRA, CRC, Regulatory Affairs specialist, or Biostatistician depending on document type.']
  authored_date date [note: 'The date on which authorship of this document version was completed and the document was submitted for review. Part of the ALCOA+ audit trail for controlled document lifecycle.']
  capa_reference varchar [note: 'The CAPA identifier from MasterControl that triggered or is associated with this document version update. Null if the version was not CAPA-driven. Enables traceability between quality events and document changes.']
  change_reason varchar [note: 'The documented business or regulatory reason that triggered the creation of this new version (e.g., protocol amendment, regulatory agency feedback, CAPA-driven update, periodic review). Supports change control traceability.']
  change_summary varchar [note: 'A concise narrative description of the changes made in this version relative to the immediately preceding version. Required for controlled document change control and regulatory inspection readiness.']
  change_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the nature of changes in this version. \'major\' = substantive content changes requiring re-training; \'minor\' = non-substantive content updates; \'administrative\' = formatting, typo, or metadata corrections only; \'initial\' = first version']
  checksum_hash varchar [note: 'The SHA-256 cryptographic hash of the document file content at the time of this version\'s creation. Used to verify document integrity and detect unauthorized alterations, supporting 21 CFR Part 11 audit trail and ALCOA+ integrity requirements.']
  confidentiality_level varchar [note: 'The data classification level assigned to this document version, governing access controls and distribution restrictions within Veeva Vault. Aligns with the organization\'s data classification policy and GDPR/HIPAA requirements.']
  country_code varchar [note: 'The ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code indicating the regulatory jurisdiction for which this document version was prepared or filed (e.g., USA, GBR, DEU, JPN). Null for globally applicable documents.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp when this document version record was first created in the source system (Veeva Vault). Part of the ALCOA+ contemporaneous audit trail. Stored in ISO 8601 format with timezone offset.']
  document_number varchar [note: 'The externally-known controlled document number or identifier (e.g., SOP-CLN-0042, TMF-PROT-001). Serves as the business-facing identifier used in regulatory submissions, audit trails, and cross-references within the Trial Master File.']
  document_title varchar [note: 'The full official title of the document as it appears on the controlled document itself. Used for display, search, and regulatory binder indexing within the eTMF.']
  document_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the document by its functional type within the TMF or SOP library (e.g., Protocol, Informed Consent Form, Investigator Brochure, SOP, Regulatory Submission, Site Agreement, Safety Report).']
  effective_date date [note: 'The date on which this document version becomes officially effective and binding for use. For SOPs, this is the date from which staff must comply with the procedure. For regulatory documents, this is the date of regulatory approval or acknowledgement.']
  expiry_date date [note: 'The date on which this document version expires and must be reviewed, renewed, or superseded. Null indicates no scheduled expiry. Critical for SOP periodic review cycles and regulatory document validity tracking.']
  file_format varchar [note: 'The electronic file format of the document version as stored in Veeva Vault (e.g., PDF, DOCX, XLSX, XML). PDF is the standard for approved controlled documents per eCTD and 21 CFR Part 11 requirements.']
  file_size_kb varchar [note: 'The size of the document version file in kilobytes as stored in Veeva Vault. Used for storage management, eTMF completeness validation, and detecting potentially corrupt or empty document uploads.']
  inspection_readiness_status varchar [note: 'Assessment of whether this document version is ready for regulatory inspection. \'ready\' = document is complete, approved, and filed correctly; \'gap_identified\' = a filing or completeness gap has been identified; \'remediation_in_progress\' = gap is being']
  language_code varchar [note: 'The ISO 639-1 language code of the document version (e.g., \'en\', \'fr\', \'de\', \'ja\'). Critical for multi-country trials where documents must be translated and filed in local languages per regulatory requirements.']
  last_modified_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp of the most recent modification to this document version record in the source system. Supports audit trail completeness and change detection in the Silver Layer ETL pipeline.']
  number varchar [note: 'The human-readable version label for this document version (e.g., 1.0, 2.1, 3.0). Follows the organization\'s controlled document versioning convention. Major increments typically indicate substantive content changes; minor increments indicate']
  regulatory_authority varchar [note: 'The regulatory authority to which this document version is relevant or was submitted (e.g., FDA, EMA, PMDA, MHRA, TGA, Health Canada). Supports regulatory submission tracking and jurisdiction-specific compliance reporting.']
  retention_expiry_date date [note: 'The date after which this document version may be destroyed per the applicable regulatory retention schedule. Calculated based on study completion date plus the required retention period (e.g., 15 years post-study for ICH GCP, 2 years post-NDA approval']
  reviewer_name varchar [note: 'Full name of the quality reviewer or subject matter expert who reviewed this document version prior to approval. Supports the QA review step in the controlled document workflow.']
  study_protocol_number varchar [note: 'The sponsor-assigned protocol number of the clinical study to which this document version is associated, if applicable. Null for enterprise-level SOPs not tied to a specific study. Enables study-level TMF completeness reporting.']
  superseded_date date [note: 'The date on which this document version was superseded by a newer approved version. Null if the version is still current or was never approved. Used to determine the active version at any point in time for historical audit queries.']
  tmf_section varchar [note: 'The specific section or artifact number within the DIA TMF Reference Model zone (e.g., 01.01, 02.03, 05.07). Used for precise eTMF filing, completeness tracking, and inspection readiness reporting.']
  tmf_zone varchar [note: 'The DIA TMF Reference Model zone to which this document belongs. Zone 1 = Trial Management; Zone 2 = Central Trial Documents; Zone 3 = Regulatory; Zone 4 = Investigational Product; Zone 5 = Site Management.']
  training_completion_deadline date [note: 'The date by which all required staff must complete training on this document version. Null if training is not required. Used to monitor training compliance and flag overdue training in MasterControl.']
  training_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether staff training is required upon approval of this document version. True for major version changes to SOPs and GCP-critical documents. Drives training assignment workflows in MasterControl.']
  vault_document_version_reference varchar [note: 'The native document version identifier assigned by Veeva Vault (eTMF/QMS module). Used to trace this Silver Layer record back to its source system record for reconciliation and audit purposes.']
  vault_lifecycle_state varchar [note: 'The native lifecycle state label as recorded in Veeva Vault for this document version (e.g., \'Draft\', \'In Review\', \'Approved\', \'Superseded\'). Preserved from the source system to enable reconciliation between the Silver Layer and Veeva Vault.']
  version_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of this document version within the controlled document workflow. \'draft\' = under authorship; \'in_review\' = circulated for review/approval; \'approved\' = effective and in use; \'superseded\' = replaced by a newer approved version']

  Note: 'Tracks the full version history of every controlled document in the TMF and SOP library. Each record represents a discrete version of a document, capturing version number, effective date, expiry date, version status (draft, in-review, approved'

  mastercontrol_doc_reference varchar [note: 'Native document identifier assigned by MasterControl (the system of record for controlled documents). Used for cross-system traceability and integration with MasterControl training, CAPA, and audit modules.']

Table document.workflow {
  workflow_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique surrogate identifier for each document workflow instance in the Databricks Silver Layer. Primary key for the document_workflow data product.']

  document_sop_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to document.document_sop. Business justification: SOPs undergo formal review, approval, and distribution workflows governed by the document_workflow entity.']
  regulatory_binder_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to document.regulatory_binder. Business justification: Workflow tracks the lifecycle of documents through review, approval, and distribution processes.']
  site_file_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to document.site_file. Business justification: Workflow tracks document lifecycle including site file review, completeness assessment, and inspection readiness workflows.']
  study_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the clinical study associated with this document workflow. Enables study-level aggregation of document control activities for inspection readiness and TMF completeness reporting.']
  study_site_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to site.study_site. Business justification: Many document workflows are site-specific: site file reviews, site-level regulatory submissions, site activation document packages, and closeout document processing.']
  tmf_document_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the controlled document record that this workflow instance governs. Links the workflow to the specific Trial Master File (TMF) or SOP document undergoing review, approval, or distribution.']
  version_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to document.document_version. Business justification: Document workflows govern a specific version of a document through its review and approval lifecycle.']

  archival_date date [note: 'Date on which the document was formally archived in the eTMF system following workflow completion. Null until archival is executed. Used to confirm compliance with ICH GCP and regulatory retention period requirements.']
  archival_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the document must be archived upon workflow completion per ICH GCP retention requirements. Drives post-approval archival workflow initiation in Veeva Vault for long-term TMF retention compliance.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when this document_workflow record was first created in the Databricks Silver Layer. Serves as the system audit creation timestamp for data lineage and ETL traceability.']
  current_step_name varchar [note: 'Name of the active step within the workflow at the time of record capture (e.g., \'Quality Review\', \'Medical Review\', \'Regulatory Approval\', \'Final Sign-Off\'). Identifies where in the process the document currently resides.']

  document_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the document being processed (e.g., \'Protocol\', \'Informed Consent Form (ICF)\', \'Investigator Brochure\', \'SOP\', \'Regulatory Submission\', \'Site File\'). Aligns with DIA TMF Reference Model artifact taxonomy.']
  electronic_signature_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether one or more steps in this workflow require a 21 CFR Part 11 compliant electronic signature. Drives system enforcement of e-signature capture and audit trail requirements in Veeva Vault.']

  escalation_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this workflow instance has been formally escalated due to non-response, SLA breach, or rejection requiring management intervention. True triggers escalation notifications to supervisory roles per the workflow escalation policy.']
  escalation_reason varchar [note: 'Categorized reason for workflow escalation. Supports root cause analysis of document control bottlenecks and informs process improvement initiatives for GCP-compliant document management.']
  escalation_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the workflow was formally escalated. Populated only when escalation_flag is True. Used to measure escalation response time and track resolution of escalated document control issues.']
  gcp_critical_document_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the document is classified as a GCP essential document per ICH E6(R2) Section 8. Critical documents require mandatory workflow completion before study activities can proceed and are prioritized in inspection readiness reviews.']
  initiated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the document workflow instance was first created and launched in Veeva Vault. Serves as the principal business event timestamp for the workflow lifecycle and the start point for overall cycle time measurement.']
  inspection_readiness_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this workflow and its associated document have been reviewed and confirmed as inspection-ready per GCP and regulatory authority standards. Supports pre-inspection TMF completeness assessments by FDA, EMA, MHRA, or other regulatory bodies.']
  instance_reference varchar [note: 'Externally-known unique identifier assigned by Veeva Vault to this specific workflow instance. Used for cross-system traceability and audit trail correlation with the source eTMF system.']
  priority_level varchar [note: 'Business priority assigned to this workflow instance, reflecting urgency of document review and approval. Critical priority is assigned to GCP essential documents, regulatory submissions with imminent deadlines, and safety-related documents.']
  regulatory_submission_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the document being processed through this workflow is intended for regulatory submission (e.g., IND, NDA, BLA, MAA, eCTD). True triggers additional compliance checks and approval requirements per FDA/EMA submission standards.']
  rejection_count varchar [note: 'Number of times the document has been rejected and returned for revision within this workflow instance. High rejection counts indicate document quality issues and are tracked for quality metrics and CAPA (Corrective and Preventive Action) analysis.']
  rejection_reason varchar [note: 'Free-text or categorized reason provided when a workflow step is rejected. Documents the specific deficiency identified by the reviewer, supporting document quality improvement and GCP audit trail requirements.']
  sla_breach_indicator boolean [note: 'Flag indicating whether the workflow or any of its steps has exceeded the defined Service Level Agreement (SLA) timeframe. True when step_completion_date or actual_completion_date exceeds the corresponding due date. Drives escalation and KPI reporting.']

  step_completion_date date [note: 'Actual date on which the current or most recently completed workflow step was actioned and closed. Compared against step_due_date to determine SLA compliance and cycle time analytics.']
  step_completion_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Precise date and time at which the workflow step action was recorded in Veeva Vault. Provides sub-day granularity required for 21 CFR Part 11 electronic audit trail and time-stamped electronic signature records.']
  step_due_date date [note: 'Target completion date for the current workflow step as defined by the workflow SLA configuration. Used to calculate SLA breach status and trigger escalation notifications for overdue document reviews.']
  target_completion_date date [note: 'Overall target date by which the entire document workflow (all steps) must be completed. Derived from workflow SLA rules and used for inspection readiness tracking and TMF completeness KPI reporting.']
  template_name varchar [note: 'Name of the Veeva Vault workflow template used to instantiate this workflow (e.g., \'SOP Review and Approval\', \'Regulatory Document Approval\', \'ICF Review Workflow\'). Identifies the standard process blueprint applied.']
  template_version varchar [note: 'Version identifier of the workflow template at the time this workflow instance was initiated. Ensures reproducibility and audit traceability when templates are updated over time.']
  tmf_zone varchar [note: 'DIA TMF Reference Model zone classification for the document being processed. Categorizes the document into the appropriate TMF structural zone to support inspection readiness and TMF completeness assessments.']
  total_steps varchar [note: 'Total number of steps defined in the workflow template for this workflow instance. Used in conjunction with current_step_sequence to calculate workflow completion percentage for inspection readiness dashboards.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when this document_workflow record was last modified in the Databricks Silver Layer. Tracks the most recent state change for incremental processing and audit trail completeness.']
  workflow_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of the document workflow instance within Veeva Vault. Tracks progression from initiation through review, approval decision, and terminal states. Supports GCP-compliant document control audit trails.']
  workflow_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the workflow by its primary business purpose within the document lifecycle. Distinguishes review-only workflows from approval workflows, distribution workflows, archival workflows, and amendment workflows.']

  Note: 'Tracks the lifecycle workflow state of a document through its review, approval, and distribution process within Veeva Vault. Captures workflow instance ID, workflow template name, current workflow step, step assignee role, step due date, step completion'
}

  reference_number varchar [note: 'Externally-known unique business identifier for the electronic signature event, as assigned by Veeva Vault or the controlling eTMF system. Used for cross-system traceability and regulatory inspection referencing.']
